articles/api-authentication.html.title: API Authentication | Organizor
articles/api-authentication.html.summary: API Authentication Overview The API accepts Keycloak JWTs from a controlled set of realms, not from arbitrary OpenID Connect issuers: the configured platform realm (organizor-dev locally); the realm mapped to an active catalog tenant, such as tenant-pjsabbe or tenant-tvdk. The API checks the catalog mapping before fetching OpenID metadata or signing keys. A token cannot make the API contact an arbitrary issuer URL. JWT Validation Every accepted token must be: signed by the allow-listed realm's keys; issued by that exact realm; unexpired; addressed to the organizor-api audience. OpenID metadata and signing keys are cached per trusted issuer. The active tenant realm mapping is checked on authentication so a soft-deleted tenant's already-issued token is rejected immediately by the API. Roles And Issuers organizor-admin is a platform role. It grants platform administration only when issued by the platform realm. tenant-admin and tenant-user are tenant-realm roles. A tenant realm cannot gain platform access merely by defining a role named organizor-admin. The platform portal uses a single platform-realm login. The backend master-realm service account is never used as a browser login. Service Accounts The master-realm organizor-provisioner client is used only by the backend to call Keycloak Admin REST endpoints. Its secret must never be sent to a browser. An internal organizor-api service account does not bypass issuer binding by itself. It must satisfy the same issuer-aware route policy as any other caller; cross-tenant support remains restricted to a platform-realm organizor-admin identity. Error Codes 401 Unauthorized: missing, expired, invalidly signed, unknown-issuer, or wrong-audience token. 403 Forbidden: valid token from the wrong tenant realm or without the required role. 400 Bad Request: missing or invalid tenant header on a tenant-scoped route.

articles/api-integration.html.title: API Integration — Platform Portal And Tenant Clients | Organizor
articles/api-integration.html.summary: API Integration — Platform Portal And Tenant Clients The Blazor portal communicates with the Organizor API through named HTTP clients. The central portal is an Organizor-admin control plane; tenant websites and tenant-admin portal hosts are separate clients with their own Keycloak realm configuration. Local Development Configuration Setting Value Portal origin https://localhost:7025 TVDK tenant-admin portal origin https://localhost:7022 API base URL https://localhost:7184 Authorized API URL https://localhost:7184 Platform token issuer https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev Platform portal OIDC client organizor-ui The API derives trusted issuers from Keycloak:BaseUrl, Keycloak:PlatformRealm, and active catalog tenant realms. It accepts platform portal tokens from the platform issuer and tenant tokens only from the realm mapped to the selected tenant. HTTPS and HTTP Keycloak endpoints are different issuers; using a different scheme causes 401 Unauthorized. HttpClient Registration The portal registers the authenticated API client in Program.cs: builder.Services.AddHttpClient("api", client => { client.BaseAddress = new Uri("https://localhost:7184"); }) .AddHttpMessageHandler<ApiAuthorizationMessageHandler>(); AdminTenantService uses IHttpClientFactory.CreateClient("api") to call platform-control-plane endpoints. Anonymous public registration uses the separate public-api client without the authorization message handler. Authorization Handler ApiAuthorizationMessageHandler extends Blazor's AuthorizationMessageHandler. It is responsible for: configuring the authorized API URL; requesting portal OIDC scopes; attaching the platform access token to outgoing requests. The handler is registered in DI and configured once in its constructor. This matters because AuthorizationMessageHandler.ConfigureHandler(...) can only be called once per handler instance. Calling ConfigureHandler(...) again for the same handler instance can cause this runtime error: handler already configured Keep handler configuration inside the handler constructor or inside the AddHttpMessageHandler factory, but not both. The current branch uses the constructor approach. The platform portal does not derive a tenant boundary from a tenant claim. Platform administration routes select a tenant by catalog id in their path. A tenant-specific client must send X-Tenant-Slug only for its own known tenant environment; the API still verifies that header against the token issuer. Tenant boundary: the tenant claim is compatibility data only and is never an authorization boundary. The API binds a tenant-scoped request to the catalog-owned realm for the supplied tenant header. Platform Tenant API Client AdminTenantService wraps the admin tenant API surface used by /admin/tenants and /admin/plans. All of these endpoints require a platform-realm organizor-admin token. Method Endpoint Purpose GetTenantsAsync GET /api/admin/tenants Loads all tenants, including soft-deleted records. OnboardAsync POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard Creates the catalog tenant, provisions its Keycloak realm, creates the database, and applies migrations. UpgradeAsync POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/upgrade Runs pending migrations for the tenant database. SoftDeleteAsync DELETE /api/admin/tenants/{id} Disables the tenant realm, then marks the tenant deleted without dropping the database. HardDeleteAsync POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/hard-delete Deletes the complete tenant realm, then drops the database and catalog record after soft deletion. GetConfigAsync GET /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config Loads the tenant's effective config after plan defaults and overrides are resolved. GetConfigOverridesAsync GET /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config-overrides Loads explicit tenant-level config overrides. UpdateConfigOverridesAsync PUT /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config-overrides Updates tenant-level config overrides. GetPlansAsync GET /api/admin/tenant-plans Loads tenant plan defaults. UpdatePlanAsync PUT /api/admin/tenant-plans/{planKey} Updates tenant plan defaults. tenant user methods /api/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/users/* Manages users inside the selected tenant realm from the platform control plane. The backend also exposes GET /api/admin/tenants/{id} for admin detail lookups. The current portal grid does not call that endpoint directly. 401 Unauthorized means the token is missing, invalid, from an untrusted issuer, or lacks the organizor-api audience. 403 Forbidden means the token is valid but lacks the platform-realm organizor-admin role. GET /api/v1/tenants is a platform-only catalog read and returns only non-deleted records. GET /api/admin/tenants intentionally includes soft-deleted records so the portal can show deleted tenants and allow hard deletion. Tenant-realm identities cannot use either route to discover or enumerate other tenants. Tenant-Scoped API Clients Tenant user-management, tenant configuration, activity, people, and registration APIs are tenant-scoped. A caller needs: a token from that tenant's catalog-owned realm; the required realm-local role (tenant-admin or tenant-user); X-Tenant-Slug for the matching tenant where the route requires a header. For example, a tenant-pjsabbe token with X-Tenant-Slug: tvdk is rejected with 403 Forbidden. A platform-realm organizor-admin is the explicit centralized-support exception where the endpoint policy permits it. The central Blazor portal is not a tenant-realm OIDC client. A tenant-admin uses the same Portal codebase at their tenant's configured host, which resolves a realm-local portal client before OIDC begins. The API message handler sends X-Tenant-Slug for tenant-scoped paths after login; the API then verifies it against the token issuer. Tenant self-service account-action endpoints act only on the caller's own identity in the matching tenant realm. A platform administrator manages another tenant user through /api/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/users, never through that user's self-service account-action route. Static Tenant Website API Contract Tenant-specific websites must first call: GET /api/public/tenants/{slug}/auth The response contains the tenant's own Keycloak authority, generated client id, PKCE requirement, scopes, redirect metadata, tenant header name, tenant claim name, expected tenant roles, realm-local group paths, and public registration endpoint. This endpoint intentionally returns no secrets. A tenant website fetches it during startup, before registering its OIDC client; it must not use the central portal's organizor-dev authority or organizor-ui client as a fallback. After login, a tenant website sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and X-Tenant-Slug: {slug} on tenant-scoped authenticated API calls. It must use the authority returned by the contract rather than hard-coding the platform realm. Before starting login, it should also verify that its own callback URL, logout URL, and browser origin occur in the returned allow-lists; a mismatch means the tenant needs corrected onboarding/auth settings. Tenant Admin Portal Runtime Contract At any Portal host other than Portal:PlatformBaseUrl, the browser starts by calling: GET /api/public/tenant-portals/auth?baseUrl={url-encoded-current-base-url} The anonymous response contains the resolved tenant slug, tenant realm authority, separate tenant-{slug}-portal client id, tenant website base URL, PKCE/scopes, and exact login/logout/origin values. It contains no client secret or Keycloak administration details. The Portal must reject a mismatch rather than falling back to the platform client. Public Registration API Client PublicRegistrationService wraps POST /api/public/register for the temporary /register shell. It uses the named public-api client instead of the authenticated api client because registration is anonymous and the tenant slug is supplied in the request body. The future tenant-specific static websites should reuse the same public registration contract with their own UI. Anonymous public form endpoints are rate limited by endpoint, tenant, and client address. A limited request returns 429 Too Many Requests with error code PUBLIC_FORM_RATE_LIMITED. Local development limits can be configured with dotnet user-secrets under: PublicFormRateLimit:ActivityRegistration:PermitLimit PublicFormRateLimit:ActivityRegistration:WindowMinutes PublicFormRateLimit:TenantUserRegistration:PermitLimit PublicFormRateLimit:TenantUserRegistration:WindowMinutes Error Handling The tenant API client uses EnsureSuccessAsync to surface failed API responses as InvalidOperationException. The exception message includes the status code and response body when present. The Radzen tenant page catches those exceptions and displays both a page alert and a Radzen notification. Troubleshooting Symptom Likely cause Fix handler already configured The same AuthorizationMessageHandler instance was configured more than once. Configure the handler in one place only. The current branch configures it in ApiAuthorizationMessageHandler's constructor. 401 Unauthorized while logged in Token issuer is not the configured platform realm or an active catalog tenant realm, its audience is wrong, or no token was attached. Align Keycloak:BaseUrl with the token issuer's HTTPS base URL, verify the correct realm client, and request an organizor-api audience token. 403 Forbidden while logged in The token has the wrong issuer/tenant pairing or lacks the issuer-appropriate role. Use a platform organizor-admin token for platform routes, or a matching tenant realm token for tenant routes. Tenant-scoped API returns bad tenant errors Tenant header is missing or invalid. Send the tenant's known slug in X-Tenant-Slug; do not rely on a tenant claim as proof of access.

articles/api.html.title: API Behavior | Organizor
articles/api.html.summary: API Behavior This page covers the platform catalog endpoints, tenant config read endpoint, and development utility endpoints. Feature-specific API surfaces are split into focused pages: Public Website API covers anonymous tenant website auth discovery and tenant-user self-registration. Tenant Domain API covers people, relationships, organizations, activities, registrations, and document capabilities. Internal Operations covers platform administration endpoints. Tenant Modules covers the code-deployed catalog, plan entitlements, tenant installations, and module operator endpoints. Tenant catalog endpoints are platform/control-plane routes, so tenant resolution does not require X-Tenant-Slug for them. They require a platform-realm organizor-admin token: POST /api/v1/tenants requires the platform-realm organizor-admin role. GET /api/v1/tenants and GET /api/v1/tenants/{slug} require the platform-realm organizor-admin role. Tenant administrators and tenant users cannot enumerate the catalog or inspect another tenant through these routes. They use their own tenant-scoped API routes and the public auth-discovery contract instead. Tenant-scoped application endpoints, including GET /api/v1/tenant/config, must include the X-Tenant-Slug header unless the path explicitly documents a different tenant selection mechanism. The API verifies that a tenant token's issuer is the catalog-owned realm for that header; the tenant claim is not used as the isolation boundary. Tenant Catalog Create Tenant POST /api/v1/tenants Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Content-Type: application/json { "name": "Acme", "slug": "acme" } Creates a catalog tenant record with Pending status, assigns its immutable IdentityRealm, and returns tenant metadata. This route does not provision a Keycloak realm, a default tenant admin, or a tenant database. Use POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard for the full onboarding workflow. Example response: { "id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111", "name": "Acme", "slug": "acme", "databaseName": "organizor_tenant_acme", "createdAt": "2026-06-09T10:30:00Z", "status": "Pending", "failureReason": null, "isDeleted": false } All tenant catalog responses use the same shape: Field Meaning id Tenant catalog identifier. name Human-readable tenant name. slug Stable slug used for lookup and tenant routing. databaseName Tenant database name assigned by the catalog. createdAt UTC catalog creation timestamp. status Current lifecycle status, such as Pending, Active, Failed, or Deleted. failureReason Provisioning or lifecycle failure detail when available. isDeleted Whether the catalog record has been soft-deleted. Public reads exclude deleted records. Possible responses: Status Meaning 200 OK Tenant catalog record was created. 401 Unauthorized Missing or invalid bearer token. 403 Forbidden Token does not satisfy the organizor-admin role policy. 409 Conflict Duplicate tenant slug. 500 Internal Server Error Unexpected server error. See Errors and Observability. Get Tenant By Slug GET /api/v1/tenants/acme Authorization: Bearer <token> Returns a tenant by slug using the tenant catalog response shape above, or 404 Not Found when no tenant exists. Soft-deleted tenants are excluded. Only a platform organizor-admin can call this route. List Tenants GET /api/v1/tenants Authorization: Bearer <token> Returns all catalog tenants visible to the platform control plane using the tenant catalog response shape above. Soft-deleted tenants are excluded. Tenant-realm identities have no catalog-list visibility. Tenant Config GET /api/v1/tenant/config Authorization: Bearer <tenant-token> X-Tenant-Slug: acme Returns the current tenant's effective config. Effective config is resolved from the tenant's assigned plan defaults plus tenant-specific overrides. This endpoint requires a matching tenant-realm tenant-admin or the platform-realm organizor-admin support exception through the issuer-aware RequireTenantAdminRole policy. Tenant access middleware also verifies that the authenticated token issuer matches the realm identified by X-Tenant-Slug. Platform Endpoints Endpoint Purpose /health Public health check endpoint. /openapi/v1.json OpenAPI document in development. /scalar Interactive OpenAPI/Scalar endpoint explorer in development. OpenAPI And Scalar When the API runs in development: OpenAPI JSON is available at /openapi/v1.json. Scalar is available at /scalar. Use this article for behavior: routes, authorization expectations, tenant headers, response shapes, and operational meaning. Use the generated API reference only for C# type signatures.

articles/architecture.html.title: Architecture | Organizor
articles/architecture.html.summary: Architecture Organizor follows a layered structure around tenant management. flowchart LR Client[HTTP client] --> Api[Code7Dev.Organizor.Api] Api --> Application[Code7Dev.Organizor.Application] Application --> Domain[Code7Dev.Organizor.Domain] Application --> Infrastructure[Code7Dev.Organizor.Infrastructure] Api --> Quartz[Quartz scheduler] Quartz --> Infrastructure Infrastructure --> Catalog[(Catalog database)] Infrastructure --> TenantDb[(Tenant databases)] API Layer The API project owns transport concerns: controller routes for platform tenant catalog operations, public tenant contracts, and internal tenant operations; request and response DTOs; mapping between API DTOs and application models; correlation ID, exception handling, and tenant resolution middleware; Serilog request logging; CORS, health checks, OpenAPI, and Scalar setup. The startup flow in Program.cs composes the application by registering catalog persistence, tenant persistence, application services, infrastructure services, and API services. Application Layer The application project owns use cases and contracts. It defines interfaces for repository access, tenant database management, migration, provisioning, onboarding, upgrades, lifecycle operations, tenant config resolution, config overrides, and plan management. Current services: Service Responsibility TenantService Creates catalog tenant records and supports platform-control-plane reads by slug or list. TenantOnboardingService Creates a catalog tenant, runs provisioning, and marks the tenant active or failed. TenantLifecycleService Soft-deletes tenants and hard-deletes already soft-deleted tenants. TenantUpgradeService Runs migrations for an existing tenant database. TenantConfigResolver Resolves effective tenant config from plan defaults plus tenant overrides. TenantConfigManagementService Reads and updates tenant-specific config overrides. TenantPlanManagementService Reads and updates tenant plan defaults. Domain Layer The domain project contains the tenant entity, tenant plan entity, tenant feature-settings value object, and tenant status enum. A tenant stores identity, immutable Keycloak realm mapping, slug, database name, plan key, config overrides, creation date, lifecycle status, provisioning failure reason, and deletion metadata. Tenant plans store reusable defaults for feature limits and behavior. Infrastructure Layer The infrastructure project owns external resources: CatalogDbContext stores tenant records. OrganizorDbContext connects to the current tenant database after tenant resolution. TenantRepository implements catalog tenant persistence. TenantPlanRepository implements tenant plan persistence. ConnectionStringBuilder builds PostgreSQL connection strings from configuration. TenantDatabaseManager creates and drops tenant databases. TenantMigrator applies EF Core migrations to tenant databases. Keycloak infrastructure provisions, disables, and deletes catalog-owned tenant realms through the backend master-realm provisioner. TenantProvisioningWorkflow creates a tenant database and applies migrations during onboarding. TenantJobScheduler schedules tenant-scoped Quartz jobs from catalog tenant records. TenantAwareJobFactory creates Quartz jobs through dependency injection. SyncTenantJob runs recurring tenant synchronization work with ITenantContext populated from Quartz job data. Background Jobs Quartz is registered by the API layer and backed by persistent PostgreSQL storage in the catalog database. On startup, the application schedules a recurring synchronization job for each catalog tenant. Each job carries the tenant ID and slug in Quartz job data, then sets the tenant context before running tenant database work. Request Pipeline sequenceDiagram participant Client participant Api participant TenantResolution participant Application participant Infrastructure Client->>Api: HTTP request Api->>Api: Correlation ID and exception handling Api->>TenantResolution: Resolve tenant when required TenantResolution->>Infrastructure: Load tenant by X-Tenant-Slug Infrastructure-->>TenantResolution: Tenant record TenantResolution->>Application: Continue with current tenant context Application->>Infrastructure: Use catalog or tenant database services Infrastructure-->>Application: Result Application-->>Api: Model Api-->>Client: HTTP response

articles/authentication-flow.html.title: Authentication Flow — Platform And Tenant-Admin Portals | Organizor
articles/authentication-flow.html.summary: Authentication Flow — Platform And Tenant-Admin Portals The Blazor Portal has two host-selected modes. The configured control-plane host uses the platform realm (organizor-dev locally) for organizor-admin users. A tenant-admin host resolves its own active tenant before OIDC starts, then uses that tenant's realm-local portal client. It is not a shared tenant login screen. PJsabbe, TVDK, and later tenants have separate Keycloak realms, identities, credentials, and sessions. Platform Login Flow An Organizor administrator clicks Login or navigates to a protected control-plane route. The portal redirects to the platform realm at https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev. Keycloak validates the platform administrator's credentials. Keycloak redirects back to https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback. Blazor WebAssembly stores the authenticated state and access token. KeycloakClaimsPrincipalFactory maps platform realm roles into Blazor role claims. RoleRedirector sends a platform organizor-admin to the control-plane shell. Tenant-Admin Login Flow A tenant administrator opens that tenant's configured portal host, for example https://localhost:7022 for TVDK. Before OIDC is registered, the Portal calls GET /api/public/tenant-portals/auth?baseUrl=... using its actual base URL. The API resolves one active tenant by its catalog-owned portal URL and returns only public OIDC configuration. The Portal verifies its base URL, callback URL, logout URL, and origin match the contract exactly, then starts Authorization Code Flow with PKCE against that tenant realm. Keycloak redirects back to the same tenant portal host. A matching tenant-admin is sent to /tenant and can use the tenant administration screens. The tenant portal never selects a realm from a username, query string, or route. An unknown host fails startup rather than falling back to the platform realm. Role Redirects Portal mode Role and issuer Redirect target Platform host Platform-realm organizor-admin /admin Platform host Any tenant identity /access-denied Tenant host Matching tenant-realm tenant-admin /tenant Tenant host Matching tenant-realm tenant-user That tenant's public website Tenant host Platform issuer or tenant mismatch /access-denied Tenant administrators and tenant users do not sign in to the central portal with the platform client. A tenant website starts OIDC from its own host after loading GET /api/public/tenants/{slug}/auth, so TVDK uses tenant-tvdk and tenant-tvdk-web rather than organizor-dev and organizor-ui. The tenant-admin portal instead uses tenant-tvdk-portal. Switching a running platform WebAssembly OIDC registration to a realm selected by query string is not supported. Logout is initiated by LogoutButton or the /logout route. Both call Blazor WebAssembly authentication through NavigateToLogout("authentication/logout", "/"), which clears local authentication state and returns the browser to the active Portal host after its matching realm logout. Role Claims The portal role factory maps roles from the platform token's realm_access.roles claim into ClaimTypes.Role. The local platform import maps the organizor-api audience so platform API calls carry the audience required by the API. Tenant website clients emit their own realm roles (tenant-admin or tenant-user), the organizor-api audience, and a tenant compatibility claim. The tenant claim is not an authorization boundary; the API binds a tenant request to the token issuer and catalog-owned tenant realm. Protected Routes The supported central portal routes require the platform role: @attribute [Authorize(Roles = "organizor-admin")] Route area Required role and issuer /admin platform organizor-admin /admin/tenants platform organizor-admin /admin/plans platform organizor-admin /admin/users platform organizor-admin /tenant and its child routes matching tenant-realm tenant-admin at the tenant portal host /register anonymous temporary test shell Tenant business routes remain API contracts protected by tenant-realm roles. The tenant portal supplies the supported browser entry point for tenant-admin; tenant-specific public websites own regular tenant-user workflows. API Tokens The portal never sends credentials to the API. It sends platform-realm bearer tokens through the configured API HttpClient. The API validates the token signature, expiry, organizor-api audience, and issuer. It accepts only the configured platform issuer or an active catalog tenant issuer. organizor-admin grants platform administration only when it comes from the platform issuer; a tenant realm cannot obtain control-plane access by using the same role name. The local platform issuer is: https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev If the portal logs in through HTTPS but the API Keycloak:BaseUrl uses the old HTTP endpoint, the issuer differs and API requests fail with 401 Unauthorized. Platform Client Requirements The platform-realm organizor-ui client must allow: Setting Value Valid redirect URI https://localhost:7025/* Web origin https://localhost:7025 Flow Standard flow / Authorization Code with PKCE Token audience organizor-api Platform users must receive organizor-admin in the platform realm before signing in. Log out and back in after a role change so the token and claims refresh. Tenant Portal Client Requirements Onboarding tenant tvdk with portal base URL https://localhost:7022 creates tenant-tvdk-portal in tenant-tvdk with these exact values: Setting Value Valid redirect URI https://localhost:7022/authentication/login-callback Post-logout redirect URI https://localhost:7022 Web origin https://localhost:7022 Flow Standard flow / Authorization Code with PKCE S256 Token audience organizor-api This client is separate from tenant-tvdk-web, even though both are public PKCE clients in the same tenant realm. Current-User Account Actions Tenant current-user account actions are realm-local API contracts. A tenant caller uses its own tenant realm token and X-Tenant-Slug; the API then performs the Keycloak operation in the matching realm. Password-change initiation is exposed as POST /api/v1/tenant/account-actions/change-password and sets Keycloak UPDATE_PASSWORD for the authenticated user. Profile update is exposed as PUT /api/v1/tenant/account-actions/profile and updates only Keycloak firstName and lastName for that realm-local user. Organizor must not collect, store, or log replacement passwords. These self-service endpoints operate only on the caller's own tenant-realm identity. Platform support manages another tenant user's identity through /api/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/users; it does not use a user's self-service account-action endpoints. The central platform portal does not provide a tenant-realm login or account screen. Tenant administrator account workflows use that tenant's portal host; regular tenant-user account workflows belong to tenant websites.

articles/background-jobs-and-docs-ops.ht.title: Background Jobs And Docs Operations | Organizor
articles/background-jobs-and-docs-ops.ht.summary: Background Jobs And Docs Operations Scheduled Tenant Jobs Organizor is wired for Quartz recurring background work, but tenant job scheduling is not currently enabled on startup. Program.cs contains a commented-out scheduling block for future use. The scheduler loads tenants from the catalog database, creates a durable SyncTenantJob per tenant, stores TenantId and TenantSlug in the Quartz job data map, and schedules or replaces the tenant trigger. Current trigger cadence: 0/10 * * * * ? That Quartz cron expression would run the tenant synchronization job every 10 seconds when scheduling is enabled. SyncTenantJob reads tenant data from the job data map, sets ITenantContext, and runs tenant-scoped work through OrganizorDbContext. The current implementation logs execution and contains placeholder synchronization work. Quartz persistence is stored in the catalog database and uses the PostgreSQL tables added by the AddQuartzTables migration. Documentation Deployment The repository contains a GitHub Actions workflow at .github/workflows/docfx-deploy.yml. On pushes to master, it checks out this repository, installs DocFX, builds docs/docfx.json, checks out the public documentation repository, copies docs/_site, commits, and pushes the generated documentation. The workflow uses the DOCS_DEPLOY_KEY secret to push to the public docs repository. Sitemap And Crawlers DocFX generates docs/_site/sitemap.xml from the build.sitemap.baseUrl value in docs/docfx.json. The documentation source includes robots.txt, which is copied into the generated site and points crawlers to the sitemap.

articles/component-structure.html.title: Portal UI Structure — High-Level | Organizor
articles/component-structure.html.summary: Portal UI Structure — High-Level The Portal UI is organized into pages, layouts, components, services, and models. The Portal selects a runtime once from its browser host. The configured platform host is the Organizor-admin control plane; a tenant portal host resolves and validates its tenant-realm configuration before OIDC starts. Tenant-admin components below are served only in that matching tenant portal mode. Pages Page Route Responsibility Home / Neutral entry page. Authenticated users can be redirected by role. Authentication /authentication/* Blazor WebAssembly OIDC login/logout callbacks. Logout /logout Convenience route that starts Blazor OIDC logout and returns to /. Admin/Dashboard /admin Admin dashboard placeholder. Admin/Tenants /admin/tenants Operational tenant catalog and lifecycle management. Admin/Plans /admin/plans Tenant plan default management. Admin/Users /admin/users?tenantId={id} Platform control-plane user management for one active tenant. TenantAdmin/Dashboard /tenant Tenant dashboard at a matching tenant portal host. TenantAdmin/Users /tenant/users Tenant-scoped user management at a matching tenant portal host. TenantAdmin/Config /tenant/config Tenant effective-config UI at a matching tenant portal host. AccessDenied /access-denied Fallback page for authenticated users without portal roles. TenantShared/Profile /tenant/profile Tenant-admin account-action UI at a matching tenant portal host. Register /register Temporary public self-registration shell. NotFound fallback Not-found page. Tenant-admin-only pages live under Pages/TenantAdmin. Tenant-admin current-user pages live under Pages/TenantShared. They require the matching tenant-local portal host/client configuration. Regular tenant-user-specific pages belong in tenant-specific public UI repositories such as TVDK, not in the Organizor portal. Layouts Layout Responsibility MainLayout General shell with login/logout controls and authenticated user context. AdminLayout Admin control-plane shell with dashboard, tenant management, plan management, current-user panel, logout, and tenant website navigation when available. TenantLayout Tenant administration shell for a matching tenant portal host; never a central-platform login target. Components Component Responsibility UserInfo Displays available username, email, tenant compatibility, and Keycloak group claims from the current authentication state. Platform users normally have no tenant context. CurrentUserPanel Sidebar user card used in admin and legacy tenant shells. Shows available display, account, and navigation context without treating tenant or groups as authorization. LogoutButton Starts Blazor OIDC logout through NavigateToLogout("authentication/logout", "/"). RoleRedirector Sends a matching platform organizor-admin from neutral entry routes to /admin, or a matching tenant-realm tenant-admin at a tenant portal host to /tenant. RedirectToLogin Sends unauthenticated users to the Blazor OIDC login route. AuthStateProvider Auth-related component wrapper used by the portal. AdminSidebar Admin navigation component retained for admin navigation reuse. UserCreateForm Shared user-create form used by platform and tenant user-management pages. UserGrid Shared user grid used by platform and tenant user-management pages. UserDetailDrawer Shared selected-user drawer with tenant access actions and removal confirmation. OrganizationEditorForm Shared grouped organization form used by focused create and selected-record edit workflows. Radzen Usage The portal references Radzen.Blazor and wires RadzenComponents in App.razor. The admin tenant page currently uses: RadzenDataGrid for tenant catalog display; RadzenTemplateForm, RadzenTextBox, RadzenTextArea, and validators for tenant onboarding and deletion input; RadzenCard for layout panels; RadzenButton for actions; RadzenBadge for tenant status; RadzenAlert and NotificationService for errors and operation feedback. Radzen services registered in Program.cs: DialogService NotificationService TooltipService ContextMenuService Services Service Responsibility UserContextService Reads AuthenticationState and maps claims into UserInfoModel. ApiAuthorizationMessageHandler Attaches the active portal token to API requests and sends X-Tenant-Slug only for a matching tenant portal context. It does not establish tenant authorization from claims. AdminTenantService Typed client for admin tenant, plan, config inspection, override, and platform user-management operations. TenantUserService Typed client for tenant user administration. TenantConfigService Typed client for tenant configuration administration. PublicRegistrationService Typed client for anonymous tenant-user self-registration from /register. PublicTenantAuthService Typed client for anonymous tenant auth discovery used to resolve the tenant website link. KeycloakClaimsPrincipalFactory Promotes Keycloak roles into Blazor role claims. Models Model Purpose UserInfoModel Display model for signed-in user context. TenantModel Portal-side tenant catalog projection. TenantOnboardingForm Validated form model for tenant onboarding. TenantOnboardingRequest API request body for onboarding. TenantSoftDeleteRequest API request body for soft deletion. TenantMigrationResult API response model for tenant database upgrades. TenantEffectiveConfigModel Effective tenant config response model used by tenant and admin config views. TenantPlanModel Tenant plan defaults model used by /admin/plans. TenantConfigOverridesModel Tenant plan assignment and override model used by /admin/tenants. TenantUserModel Portal-side Keycloak tenant-user projection. TenantUserRegistrationForm Public registration form model used by /register. TenantModel mirrors the API tenant response used by the admin grid: Id, Name, Slug, DatabaseName, CreatedAt, Status, FailureReason, and IsDeleted. Extension Rules Add page-level authorization attributes to protected pages. Keep API calls inside services instead of Razor markup. Use the named api HttpClient for backend calls so tokens are attached consistently. Avoid forcing full page reloads for internal route redirects unless a complete browser reload is required. Do not add UI for operations until the backing API route exists, unless the page is clearly marked as a placeholder.

articles/configuration.html.title: Configuration | Organizor
articles/configuration.html.summary: Configuration Organizor reads standard ASP.NET Core configuration from appsettings.json, environment-specific files, user secrets, and environment variables. Catalog Connection String CatalogDbContext expects a connection string named Catalog. Example shape: { "ConnectionStrings": { "Catalog": "Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=organizor_catalog;Username=postgres;Password=<postgres-password>" } } Tenant PostgreSQL Settings ConnectionStringBuilder builds tenant and admin connection strings from the Postgres section. { "Postgres": { "Host": "localhost", "Port": "5432", "User": "postgres", "Password": "<postgres-password>" } } The admin connection uses the postgres database. Tenant connections use the tenant database name stored in the catalog. Keycloak The API uses one Keycloak deployment but does not use one application realm for every tenant: Keycloak:PlatformRealm identifies the Organizor control-plane realm. Local development uses organizor-dev. Every active catalog tenant has its own immutable Tenant.IdentityRealm, such as tenant-pjsabbe or tenant-tvdk. Keycloak:AdminRealm identifies the realm that issues the backend provisioning token. It defaults to master. Keycloak:AdminClientId and Keycloak:AdminClientSecret identify the backend-only organizor-provisioner service account in that admin realm. The API constructs the platform issuer from Keycloak:BaseUrl and Keycloak:PlatformRealm, then accepts only that issuer and issuers of active catalog tenant realms. It validates the organizor-api audience and never follows OpenID metadata from an issuer supplied by an untrusted token. There is no API setting named Keycloak:Authority or Keycloak:Realm in this model. Example development shape: { "Keycloak": { "BaseUrl": "https://localhost:8443", "PlatformRealm": "organizor-dev", "AdminRealm": "master", "AdminClientId": "organizor-provisioner", "AdminClientSecret": "<provisioner-client-secret>", "DefaultTenantAdminTemporaryPassword": "<optional-local-only-password>", "DevelopmentAdmin": { "Username": "admin@organizor.dev", "Email": "admin@organizor.dev", "Password": "<local-only-organizor-admin-password>" } } } BaseUrl must be the canonical Keycloak HTTP(S) base URL. A mismatch between http and https changes the issuer and makes token validation fail with 401 Unauthorized. The development API accepts the local self-signed Keycloak certificate for metadata and admin-client calls. This is development-only behavior and must not be used for production identity-provider calls. Store the provisioner secret in user secrets, environment variables, or deployment secret storage. It must never appear in the portal, a tenant website, or a public auth-discovery response. Use Keycloak Setup to bootstrap the local provisioner after a Keycloak reset. Outside Development, the API refuses to start when the Keycloak base URL, platform realm, admin client id, or admin client secret is missing, non-HTTPS where required, or uses a loopback URL. Keycloak:AdminRealm is optional and defaults to master; setting it explicitly is useful for clarity or an intentionally different administration realm. Keycloak:DefaultTenantAdminTemporaryPassword is optional and supported only in Development for predictable local testing. When omitted, onboarding generates a unique temporary password for the default {slug}-admin user. Production refuses to start if this setting is configured. In Development, the API can seed the configured Keycloak:DevelopmentAdmin:Username with the platform-realm organizor-admin role when Keycloak:DevelopmentAdmin:Username, Keycloak:DevelopmentAdmin:Email, and Keycloak:DevelopmentAdmin:Password are configured. Store development-admin values in user secrets, not Docker .env files or source. Existing users keep their current password unless Keycloak:DevelopmentAdmin:ResetPasswordOnStartup is explicitly set to true. Portal UI The current Blazor WebAssembly portal is the central Organizor-admin control plane. It uses the platform realm and calls the API with platform-realm bearer tokens. The portal reads these values from wwwroot/appsettings.json or the matching environment-specific Blazor configuration file: Api:BaseUrl Portal:PlatformBaseUrl Keycloak:Authority Keycloak:ClientId Authentication:RedirectUri Authentication:PostLogoutRedirectUri Keycloak:Authority remains a browser-client setting, not an API setting. Its local value is https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev. Current local development endpoints: Setting Value Portal URL https://localhost:7025 Platform Keycloak authority https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev Portal client ID organizor-ui Login callback https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback API base URL https://localhost:7184 These values must stay aligned with the organizor-ui client redirect URIs and web origins in the platform realm. Portal:PlatformBaseUrl identifies that one fixed host. At every other Portal host, startup resolves and validates a trusted tenant-specific runtime configuration and tenant-local client through the anonymous portal auth contract; it never falls back to the platform configuration. Quartz Quartz uses the Catalog connection string for its persistent store. The same catalog database stores tenant records and Quartz scheduler tables. The API registration configures: PostgreSQL-backed Quartz persistence; Newtonsoft JSON serialization for persisted job data; clustering support; hosted service startup for Quartz background processing. Tenant job scheduling is not enabled on application startup yet. TenantJobScheduler is available for future real tenant jobs, but the startup scheduling block is currently commented out until those jobs exist. Logging Serilog is configured in appsettings.json. Current sinks: console; rolling file logs under logs/log-.txt. Log output includes tenant and request correlation properties when available: Id; Slug; DatabaseName; CorrelationId. Identity lifecycle logs additionally identify the catalog tenant realm where useful. Never log provisioner secrets or bearer tokens. CORS The API selects a CORS policy by environment: DevCors in development allows any origin, header, and method. ProdCors outside development dynamically allows origins from active tenant website configuration in the catalog. Production CORS uses tenant auth.webOrigins values and the origin of website.baseUrl as the allow-list source. Wildcards, malformed origins, URL fragments, non-origin webOrigins, and non-local HTTP origins are rejected. CORS is not authorization; bearer tokens, issuer-aware role policies, tenant resolution, and issuer-to-tenant checks still enforce API access. OpenAPI and Scalar OpenAPI and Scalar endpoints are mapped only in development. This keeps the production surface smaller while retaining local API exploration during development.

articles/database-provisioning.html.title: Database Provisioning | Organizor
articles/database-provisioning.html.summary: Database Provisioning Organizor uses one catalog database and one PostgreSQL database per tenant. Catalog Database CatalogDbContext stores tenant records in the tenants table and tenant plan definitions in the tenant_plans table. Important constraints: Field Constraint Name Required, max length 200. Slug Required, max length 100, unique index. DatabaseName Required, max length 200. PlanKey Required, max length 100, defaults to starter, references tenant_plans.key. Features Required PostgreSQL jsonb, defaults to {}. Settings Required PostgreSQL jsonb, defaults to {}. IsDeleted Required, defaults to false. DeletionReason Optional, max length 500. Important tenant_plans constraints: Field Constraint Key Required, max length 100, primary key. Name Required, max length 200. Description Optional, max length 500. Features Required PostgreSQL jsonb, defaults to {}. Settings Required PostgreSQL jsonb, defaults to {}. IsActive Required, defaults to true. SortOrder Required, defaults to 0. CreatedAt Required UTC timestamp. The tenant-config migration inserts a minimal starter plan row before adding the tenant plan foreign key. This keeps existing tenants migratable because their new PlanKey defaults to starter. After migrations are applied, startup seeding idempotently creates or updates the initial tenant plans: Plan key Purpose starter Default plan for new tenants with conservative limits. pro Larger customer plan with higher limits and more enabled features. The seed data is managed in SeedCatalogDbAsync. It runs after CatalogDbContext migrations so it can enrich the minimal migration-created starter row and add pro. Manual verification after startup: select key, name, features, settings from tenant_plans where key in ('starter', 'pro') order by sort_order; Creating or onboarding a tenant without explicit plan selection should leave tenants.plan_key set to starter. On startup, the API checks whether the catalog database exists, creates it when needed, and applies catalog migrations. The full tenant onboarding workflow is documented in Internal Operations. Database provisioning is one part of that workflow; the catalog-owned tenant Keycloak realm and its realm-local identity resources are provisioned before the tenant database is created. Tenant Database Naming Tenant databases use: organizor_tenant_{slug} Example: organizor_tenant_acme Slugs are normalized to lowercase before tenant records are written. PostgreSQL Requirements The configured PostgreSQL user must be able to: connect to the admin postgres database; create tenant databases; drop tenant databases during hard deletion; create extensions in tenant databases. Tenant database creation currently uses: CREATE DATABASE "{databaseName}" OWNER = postgres ENCODING = 'UTF8'; Each tenant database is initialized with: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "pgcrypto"; CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "citext"; Hard deletion uses: DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "{databaseName}" WITH (FORCE); Migration Flow TenantMigrator builds a tenant-specific connection string, checks pending migrations on OrganizorDbContext, applies them, and returns: Field Meaning Database Tenant database name. Success Whether migrations completed. AppliedMigrations Count of migrations pending before execution. Duration Migration runtime. Error Error message when migration fails. The active tenant migrations currently create only implemented tenant-business tables. As of tenant person relationships, that means: Table Purpose organizations Tenant-local organization records managed from the portal. activity_types Tenant-local activity type definitions managed from the portal. activity_type_document_capabilities Activity-type document capability assignments and capability-specific options. activity_type_registration_fields Registration field metadata attached to activity types. activities Tenant-local activity records with optional organization references. people Minimal participant person records required by registration submission. registrations Activity registration records and manual payment state. person_relationships Tenant-local directional relationships from a responsible/contact person to a child or related person. email_templates Tenant-local configurable email templates keyed by mail purpose and scope. email_deliveries Tenant-local email delivery attempt log keyed by mail purpose. Organization membership tables are intentionally excluded until their owning feature specs are implemented and their migrations are added. Onboarding and Cleanup During POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard, the database steps are: create the tenant database named organizor_tenant_{slug}; initialize required PostgreSQL extensions; apply pending OrganizorDbContext migrations; return success so the tenant can be marked Active. If the migration result fails or onboarding throws unexpectedly, the catalog tenant is marked Failed. During hard deletion, the tenant must already be soft-deleted. The hard-delete workflow deletes the complete tenant realm first, drops the tenant database with DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ... WITH (FORCE), and then removes the catalog record. Realm deletion failure stops the database/catalog cleanup.

articles/developer-guide.html.title: Developer Guide | Organizor
articles/developer-guide.html.summary: Developer Guide Use this page when you are returning to the repository and need the shortest reliable path back into development. Daily Loop Read the active spec under spec/features/ before changing behavior. Start local dependencies. Run the API and portal with HTTPS launch profiles. Make the smallest scoped change that matches the spec. Run targeted tests first, then a solution build before committing. Update conceptual docs when behavior changes. Local Startup From the repository root: Copy-Item .\.env.example .\.env docker compose --env-file .\.env up -d pwsh ./scripts/bootstrap-keycloak-provisioner.ps1 -SkipCertificateCheck dotnet run --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj --launch-profile https dotnet run --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui\Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui.csproj --launch-profile https On a fresh Keycloak database, Docker Compose imports the platform realm and the bootstrap script creates the backend-only master-realm organizor-provisioner service account. The script is safe to rerun and smoke-verifies its Keycloak Admin REST access without printing secrets. See Local Development before using it with a reset environment. Expected local URLs: Component URL Portal UI https://localhost:7025 API https://localhost:7184 API HTTP fallback http://localhost:5100 Keycloak https://localhost:8443 Scalar https://localhost:7184/scalar For certificate setup, reset steps, and troubleshooting, use Local Development. Verification Commands Use these commands from the repository root: dotnet build .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.slnx --no-restore -p:OutDir=C:\tmp\organizor-build\out\ dotnet test .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Tests\Code7Dev.Organizor.Tests.csproj --no-build -p:OutDir=C:\tmp\organizor-build\out\ git diff --check For a clean build without relying on a previous restore: dotnet build .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.slnx -p:OutDir=C:\tmp\organizor-build\out\ If the normal build output is locked by a running API or debugger, keep using the temporary OutDir pattern above. Tenant-Scoped API Calls Tenant-scoped API requests require both: Authorization: Bearer <token> X-Tenant-Slug: <tenant-slug> Tenant-specific clients supply their known tenant slug from their own runtime configuration or public auth contract. The API requires the token issuer to match the catalog realm for that header; a tenant token claim is compatibility data, not tenant authorization. Platform control-plane routes select tenants by catalog identifier and use a platform organizor-admin token. Anonymous public registration does not use the authenticated handler; it sends the tenant slug in the public registration request body. Documentation Rules Edit conceptual docs under docs/articles/ for workflows, behavior, setup, and integration guidance. Do not manually edit: docs/api/ docs/_site/ Those folders are generated by DocFX. Build docs locally with: docfx .\docs\docfx.json Spec Workflow Shortcut For behavior changes, follow the owning feature spec. For small wording fixes or documentation alignment, use the lightweight workflow in workflow.md instead of creating a new feature folder.

articles/errors-and-observability.html.title: Errors and Observability | Organizor
articles/errors-and-observability.html.summary: Errors and Observability Correlation IDs Every request passes through CorrelationIdMiddleware. Clients can provide a correlation ID: X-Correlation-ID: request-123 If the header is missing, the API generates a GUID. The final value is returned in the response header: X-Correlation-ID: 2ad71e7a-13cb-4ef8-a4c7-f3a37ad9dc71 The same value is pushed into Serilog context as CorrelationId. Error Shape Unhandled exceptions are returned as RFC 7807-style problem details: { "type": "https://httpstatuses.com/500", "title": "An unexpected error occurred.", "status": 500, "detail": "Exception message", "instance": "/api/v1/tenants", "correlationId": "2ad71e7a-13cb-4ef8-a4c7-f3a37ad9dc71" } The response content type is: application/problem+json Note The current middleware includes exception messages in detail. Treat that as useful during development, but review it before exposing production environments. Tenant Resolution Errors Tenant-scoped requests require: X-Tenant-Slug: acme Missing tenant slug returns 400 Bad Request with a plain text response. Unknown tenant slug returns 404 Not Found with a plain text response. Log Context Serilog output is configured to include: Property Source CorrelationId Request header or generated GUID. Id Resolved tenant ID. Slug Resolved tenant slug. DatabaseName Tenant database selection when available. SourceContext Logger source in file logs.

articles/getting-started.html.title: Getting Started | Organizor
articles/getting-started.html.summary: Getting Started For the full local topology, expected ports, startup order, and verification checklist, use Local Development. This page keeps the shorter first-run flow. Prerequisites .NET SDK 10. PostgreSQL available to the API. Keycloak available to the API. The repository includes a development Keycloak compose file. A catalog database connection string named Catalog. PostgreSQL server settings under the Postgres configuration section for tenant database creation and resolution. Keycloak bearer-token settings under the Keycloak configuration section. DocFX installed as a .NET tool when building documentation locally. Install DocFX if the docfx command is not available: dotnet tool install -g docfx Start the development Keycloak instance: Copy-Item .\.env.example .\.env docker compose --env-file .\.env up -d pwsh ./scripts/bootstrap-keycloak-provisioner.ps1 -SkipCertificateCheck The compose file starts Keycloak at https://localhost:8443. Generate and trust the local certificate first if keycloak/certs/keycloak.p12 does not exist. On a fresh Keycloak database, Compose imports the organizor-dev platform realm; the bootstrap script creates the backend-only master-realm organizor-provisioner client and verifies its Admin REST access. Tenant realms are created later by onboarding. See Keycloak Setup for API user-secret configuration. Run the API From the repository root: dotnet run --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj Development launch profiles expose: Profile URL http http://localhost:5100 https https://localhost:7184 and http://localhost:5100 On startup the API: configures Serilog; registers catalog and tenant database services; registers application and infrastructure services; seeds or migrates the catalog database; maps controllers, health checks, OpenAPI, and Scalar in development. Development Endpoints Endpoint Purpose /health ASP.NET Core health checks. /openapi/v1.json OpenAPI document, available in development. /scalar Interactive OpenAPI/Scalar endpoint explorer, available in development. Example tenant catalog request: $token = "<organizor-admin JWT>" Invoke-RestMethod ` -Method Post ` -Uri "http://localhost:5100/api/v1/tenants" ` -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $token" } ` -ContentType "application/json" ` -Body '{"name":"Acme","slug":"acme"}' POST /api/v1/tenants creates a catalog record only and requires a platform-realm organizor-admin token. Use POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard when you also need tenant realm and database provisioning. Run the Portal UI From the repository root: dotnet run --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui\Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui.csproj --launch-profile https The HTTPS profile exposes the portal at https://localhost:7025. The portal is configured to: authenticate against https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev; use the organizor-ui Keycloak client; receive login callbacks at https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback; call the API at https://localhost:7184. This is the central platform portal. Tenant websites obtain their own authority and client id from GET /api/public/tenants/{slug}/auth. After onboarding a tenant with tenantAdminPortalBaseUrl, start the same Portal project with the tenant-https profile at https://localhost:7022; it resolves the tenant realm and separate portal client from GET /api/public/tenant-portals/auth. Build the Documentation From the repository root: docfx .\docs\docfx.json DocFX writes the generated site to docs/_site and generated C# type-reference metadata to docs/api. Both folders are ignored by git and can be rebuilt.

articles/internal-operations.html.title: Internal Operations | Organizor
articles/internal-operations.html.summary: Internal Operations Internal operations are platform-control-plane workflows for tenant lifecycle, configuration, plans, scheduled jobs, and documentation deployment. An Organizor administrator uses one platform-realm organizor-admin login to manage every tenant. Tenant identities remain in separate tenant realms, and the backend alone uses the master-realm organizor-provisioner service account to operate Keycloak Admin REST APIs. The administrator does not need tenant-realm or master credentials. Use the focused pages below for implementation details: Area Details Tenant lifecycle and realm deletion order Tenant Lifecycle Operations Tenant config and plans Tenant Config Operations Portal admin workflows Portal Admin Workflows Keycloak topology and provisioner bootstrap Keycloak Setup Background jobs and docs deployment Background Jobs And Docs Operations All tenant lifecycle, config, and plan administration endpoints require a platform-issued organizor-admin token. A role of the same name from a tenant realm does not satisfy that policy. Endpoint Map Endpoint Purpose POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard Creates the catalog tenant, its identity realm, database, included modules, and—only when newly created—the one-time default tenant-admin credential (Cache-Control: no-store). GET /api/admin/tenants Lists all tenants, including soft-deleted tenants. GET /api/admin/tenants/{id} Loads one tenant by catalog ID. POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/upgrade Runs pending tenant database migrations. DELETE /api/admin/tenants/{id} Disables the tenant realm, then soft-deletes the tenant. POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/hard-delete Deletes the tenant realm, then database and catalog record for a previously soft-deleted tenant. GET /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config Inspects effective tenant config. GET /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config-overrides Loads explicit tenant overrides. PUT /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config-overrides Replaces tenant plan assignment and overrides. GET /api/admin/tenant-plans Lists tenant plans. PUT /api/admin/tenant-plans/{planKey} Replaces editable tenant plan defaults. Tenant identity realm mappings are catalog lifecycle data and are not editable through configuration or plan endpoints. Realm failures return TENANT_IDENTITY_PROVIDER_FAILED and stop destructive lifecycle work before database/catalog cleanup. The Blazor portal exposes control-plane workflows through /admin/tenants and /admin/plans; it does not bypass API authorization. Tenant-admin hosting and login use the same Portal codebase at each tenant's configured portal host, with the tenant realm resolved before OIDC begins.

articles/introduction.html.title: Introduction | Organizor
articles/introduction.html.summary: Introduction Organizor is the backend API for managing tenant environments. It keeps tenant records in a central catalog database, provisions a separate PostgreSQL database for each tenant, and gives every tenant a separate Keycloak realm for identity isolation. The current implementation focuses on tenant lifecycle operations: creating tenant catalog records; onboarding tenants by creating a tenant Keycloak realm, tenant database, and applying migrations through internal operations; resolving tenant context for tenant-scoped requests; upgrading tenant databases by running migrations; soft-deleting tenants before hard deletion; exposing health checks, OpenAPI JSON, and Scalar endpoint exploration in development. Main Concepts Concept Description Tenant A customer or isolated workspace tracked by Id, Name, Slug, immutable IdentityRealm, DatabaseName, lifecycle status, and deletion metadata. Catalog database Central PostgreSQL database that stores all tenant records. Tenant database PostgreSQL database named from the tenant slug, currently using the organizor_tenant_{slug} convention. Tenant identity realm Keycloak realm named tenant-{slug} that contains only that tenant's users, credentials, roles, groups, and clients. Platform realm Keycloak realm containing Organizor-control-plane identities and organizor-admin. Tenant resolution Middleware step that reads X-Tenant-Slug, loads the tenant, and stores the current tenant in ITenantContext. Provisioning workflow Infrastructure workflow that creates the tenant realm, tenant database, and applies tenant migrations. Project Layout Project Responsibility Code7Dev.Organizor.Api ASP.NET Core host, controllers, DTOs, mappers, middleware, OpenAPI/Scalar, health checks, CORS, and logging setup. Code7Dev.Organizor.Application Tenant service contracts, tenant models, onboarding, lifecycle, upgrade, and catalog-facing application logic. Code7Dev.Organizor.Domain Tenant entity and TenantStatus enum. Code7Dev.Organizor.Infrastructure EF Core contexts, repository implementation, PostgreSQL connection string building, database creation/deletion, migration, and tenant context storage. Documentation Boundaries The documentation is split into two intentionally different areas: Area Purpose Conceptual docs Explain behavior, workflows, configuration, security, local development, operations, and integration decisions. Generated API reference Lists C# namespaces, classes, interfaces, methods, and signatures generated from source. Do not use the generated reference to explain workflows or product behavior. Keep that content in the conceptual articles so it stays readable and can include context, examples, and operational guidance.

articles/keycloak-clients.html.title: Keycloak Clients | Organizor
articles/keycloak-clients.html.summary: Keycloak Clients Keycloak clients are scoped to their realm. Client ids may be repeated only when their realm is intentionally different; tenant website client ids remain deterministic because their tenant realm is already unique. Platform Realm Clients The local organizor-dev platform realm import creates: Client Purpose organizor-ui Public PKCE client for the central Organizor-admin portal. It emits realm roles and the organizor-api audience. organizor-api Internal API audience/service client for platform automation. The control-plane Portal host is configured only for the platform realm. It is not a username- or query-driven runtime tenant-realm switcher. Master-Realm Provisioner organizor-provisioner is created in the Keycloak master realm by scripts/bootstrap-keycloak-provisioner.ps1. It is a confidential, service-account-only client. The API uses its secret to call Keycloak Admin REST APIs for tenant realm lifecycle; no browser or tenant website uses it. API configuration: { "Keycloak": { "BaseUrl": "https://localhost:8443", "PlatformRealm": "organizor-dev", "AdminRealm": "master", "AdminClientId": "organizor-provisioner", "AdminClientSecret": "<deployment secret>" } } Tenant Realm Clients Onboarding tenant acme creates tenant-acme and configures: Client Purpose organizor-api Internal audience client required by API JWT validation. tenant-acme-web Public PKCE client for Acme's website, with the onboarding redirect URIs and origins. tenant-acme-portal Separate public PKCE client for Acme's tenant-admin portal host. Both tenant public clients: uses Authorization Code with PKCE S256; has direct grants, implicit flow, and service accounts disabled; emits realm roles, aud: organizor-api, and a direct tenant: acme compatibility claim; are deleted as part of deleting the tenant realm. Tenant websites must obtain their authority and website client id from: GET /api/public/tenants/{slug}/auth Tenant portals instead resolve their authority and portal client id by exact current base URL: GET /api/public/tenant-portals/auth?baseUrl={url-encoded-portal-base-url} Do not hard-code the old organizor-dev authority in a TVDK/PJsabbe website or tenant portal. The website and portal clients are intentionally separate even when they use the same tenant realm.

articles/keycloak-groups-users.html.title: Keycloak Groups And Users | Organizor
articles/keycloak-groups-users.html.summary: Keycloak Groups And Users Each tenant has its own Keycloak realm. Tenant identities do not use the old shared /tenants/{slug} group hierarchy. For tenant acme, onboarding creates realm tenant-acme with: realm roles tenant-admin and tenant-user; group /admins mapped to tenant-admin; group /users mapped to tenant-user; tenant website client tenant-acme-web; an internal organizor-api audience client; after successful database and included-module provisioning, default tenant admin acme-admin in /admins. The same username or email can be created in tenant-pjsabbe and tenant-tvdk because Keycloak uniqueness is realm-local. Their user IDs, credentials, sessions, and role assignments are independent. Platform Administrators Platform administrators live only in the configured platform realm (organizor-dev locally) and carry organizor-admin. They manage tenant realms through the Organizor portal and API; they do not sign into each tenant realm or the Keycloak master realm. Tenant Claims And Roles Tenant website clients emit: realm roles so tenant users receive tenant-user or tenant-admin; aud: organizor-api for API token validation; a direct tenant claim containing the tenant slug for client compatibility. The API does not use the tenant claim as its isolation boundary. It binds each tenant-scoped request to the JWT issuer and the catalog-owned tenant realm. Lifecycle Soft delete disables the tenant realm and removes it from API token issuer allow-listing. Hard delete removes the complete tenant realm, including all users, sessions, groups, roles, and clients, before deleting the tenant database and catalog record. Removing one tenant user affects only that realm-local identity. It cannot remove or disable a user in another tenant realm.

articles/keycloak-https.html.title: Keycloak HTTPS Setup | Organizor
articles/keycloak-https.html.summary: Keycloak HTTPS Setup The development Keycloak container runs over HTTPS at https://localhost:8443. The Blazor platform portal, tenant websites, and API must all use this same HTTPS base URL so their realm issuers remain canonical. The platform portal signs in through organizor-dev. Tenant realms such as tenant-pjsabbe and tenant-tvdk are created by onboarding. The API accepts only the platform issuer and active catalog tenant issuers; it does not use one static API Keycloak:Authority setting. Why HTTPS Is Required Browser applications should not mix HTTPS portal/API calls with HTTP identity-provider redirects. OIDC redirect URIs must match the browser origin exactly. Keycloak 24 runs with explicit hostname and HTTPS configuration when started in production mode. Local HTTPS keeps browser, API, and identity-provider behavior closer to production. Certificate The compose file mounts a PKCS#12 certificate from: keycloak/certs/keycloak.p12 Generate a trusted local certificate with mkcert: mkcert -install mkcert -pkcs12 -p12-file .\keycloak\certs\keycloak.p12 localhost mkcert PKCS#12 files use a local keystore password. Put that password in .env as ORGANIZOR_KEYCLOAK_HTTPS_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD so it is not committed. Keep generated certificates out of source control. If the certificate is missing or not trusted, Keycloak may fail to start or the browser may reject the login page. Docker Compose The Keycloak service uses production mode with an HTTPS keystore: keycloak: image: quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:24.0 command: - start - --hostname=localhost - --https-port=8443 - --https-key-store-file=/opt/keycloak/conf/keycloak.p12 - --https-key-store-password=${ORGANIZOR_KEYCLOAK_HTTPS_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD:?Set ORGANIZOR_KEYCLOAK_HTTPS_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD in .env} volumes: - ./keycloak/certs/keycloak.p12:/opt/keycloak/conf/keycloak.p12 ports: - "8443:8443" Start or restart Keycloak from the repository root: docker compose --env-file .\.env down docker compose --env-file .\.env up -d With an empty Keycloak database, Docker Compose imports only the platform realm resources from docker/keycloak/import/organizor-dev-realm.json. Tenant realms are created by tenant onboarding. Development Keycloak master-admin credentials are read from the untracked .env file: ORGANIZOR_KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_USERNAME / ORGANIZOR_KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD They are used only to bootstrap the backend provisioner after a reset. Organizor administrators do not need a Keycloak master login for normal work. Backend Provisioner Bootstrap After a fresh Keycloak start, run: pwsh ./scripts/bootstrap-keycloak-provisioner.ps1 -SkipCertificateCheck The script creates or updates confidential, service-account-only client organizor-provisioner in master. It assigns and explicitly scopes the master admin role, then smoke-verifies that its client-credentials token can call the Admin REST API. It does not print the client secret or bearer token. Configure the API with the matching Keycloak:BaseUrl, Keycloak:PlatformRealm, Keycloak:AdminRealm, Keycloak:AdminClientId, and Keycloak:AdminClientSecret values. See Keycloak Setup for the complete reset and secret configuration steps. Browser Trust Chrome and Edge normally trust the mkcert root certificate through the Windows certificate store after mkcert -install. If Edge still reports ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID, import the mkcert root certificate manually into Trusted Root Certification Authorities: %LOCALAPPDATA%\mkcert\rootCA.pem Then restart the browser. Expected Local Endpoints Component URL Keycloak base URL https://localhost:8443 Platform realm issuer https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev Tenant realm issuer pattern https://localhost:8443/realms/tenant-{slug} Portal UI https://localhost:7025 API HTTPS profile https://localhost:7184 The central portal's browser configuration uses the platform authority https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev. Tenant websites must use the tenant authority returned from GET /api/public/tenants/{slug}/auth. The API configuration uses the HTTPS base URL, not a fixed realm authority. Keycloak:BaseUrl must therefore be https://localhost:8443; an API configured with the old HTTP base URL rejects HTTPS-issued tokens because the issuer does not match. API User Secrets For local development, configure the API after bootstrap: dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:BaseUrl" "https://localhost:8443" --project Code7Dev.Organizor.Api/Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:PlatformRealm" "organizor-dev" --project Code7Dev.Organizor.Api/Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:AdminRealm" "master" --project Code7Dev.Organizor.Api/Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:AdminClientId" "organizor-provisioner" --project Code7Dev.Organizor.Api/Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:AdminClientSecret" "<value from .env>" --project Code7Dev.Organizor.Api/Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj Restart the API after changing these values. Running API processes keep the old configuration in memory. The development API accepts the local Keycloak certificate for metadata and admin-client calls. Browser trust is still required for portal and tenant website login. Troubleshooting Symptom Likely cause Fix Keycloak does not start Missing keycloak/certs/keycloak.p12 Generate the certificate with mkcert. Browser rejects Keycloak mkcert root CA is not trusted Run mkcert -install or import the root CA manually. Portal login redirects fail Platform client redirect URI does not include https://localhost:7025/* Update the platform-realm organizor-ui client redirect URIs. Tenant website login redirects fail The tenant website client has stale redirect URIs or authority. Re-onboard/update the tenant settings and use its public auth contract. API returns 401 for a valid token API Keycloak:BaseUrl uses HTTP, the issuer is not an active platform/tenant realm, or the audience is missing. Use https://localhost:8443, verify the tenant is active, and request an organizor-api audience token. Provisioner bootstrap fails Master admin credentials, provisioner values, or local certificate are wrong. Correct .env, wait for Keycloak startup, then rerun the script; it is safe to rerun.

articles/keycloak-setup.html.title: Keycloak Setup | Organizor
articles/keycloak-setup.html.summary: Keycloak Setup Organizor uses one Keycloak deployment and database, with identity isolation at the realm boundary: organizor-dev is the local platform realm. It contains Organizor administrators and the central portal client. tenant-{slug} is created for every tenant. For example, PJsabbe uses tenant-pjsabbe; TVDK uses tenant-tvdk. master contains the backend-only provisioning service account. It is not an application login realm. Use Keycloak HTTPS Setup before configuring clients or testing login. With an empty Keycloak database, Docker Compose imports docker/keycloak/import/organizor-dev-realm.json, which creates only platform resources. Local Provisioner Bootstrap After starting a fresh Keycloak database, create the master-realm service account used by the API: pwsh ./scripts/bootstrap-keycloak-provisioner.ps1 -SkipCertificateCheck The script reads the Keycloak admin and provisioner values from .env; it does not print the provisioner secret. Configure the API with matching user secrets: dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:BaseUrl" "https://localhost:8443" --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:PlatformRealm" "organizor-dev" --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:AdminRealm" "master" --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:AdminClientId" "organizor-provisioner" --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:AdminClientSecret" "<value from .env>" --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj The provisioner has Keycloak server-administration permissions because it must create and delete arbitrary tenant realms. Treat its client secret like production infrastructure credentials: store it only in backend deployment secrets, never in portal or tenant-website configuration. Reset Behavior docker compose --env-file .\.env down -v removes the local Keycloak database volume only. The next up -d imports the platform realm again. Run the provisioner bootstrap script again before onboarding tenants. It does not remove the Organizor catalog or tenant PostgreSQL databases; use the clearly destructive Full Local Test Reset procedure when a completely fresh test environment is intended. Focused Guides Area Details HTTPS container and certificate trust Keycloak HTTPS Setup API, platform, tenant website, and tenant-admin portal clients Keycloak Clients Tenant realm users, roles, and groups Keycloak Groups And Users Local token inspection Keycloak Token Testing API authentication behavior API Authentication Architecture flowchart TD subgraph Master[master realm] Provisioner[Backend-only provisioner service account] end subgraph Platform[organizor-dev platform realm] PlatformAdmin[organizor-admin] Portal[organizor-ui] PlatformApi[organizor-api audience] end subgraph PJsabbe[tenant-pjsabbe realm] PjUsers[PJsabbe users and admins] PjWeb[tenant-pjsabbe-web] PjPortal[tenant-pjsabbe-portal] PjApi[organizor-api audience] end subgraph TVDK[tenant-tvdk realm] TvUsers[TVDK users and admins] TvWeb[tenant-tvdk-web] TvPortal[tenant-tvdk-portal] TvApi[organizor-api audience] end Provisioner --> Platform Provisioner --> PJsabbe Provisioner --> TVDK Portal --> PlatformAdmin PjWeb --> PjUsers PjPortal --> PjUsers TvWeb --> TvUsers TvPortal --> TvUsers

articles/keycloak-token-testing.html.title: Keycloak Token Testing | Organizor
articles/keycloak-token-testing.html.summary: Keycloak Token Testing Platform token endpoint: https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev/protocol/openid-connect/token Tenant acme token endpoint: https://localhost:8443/realms/tenant-acme/protocol/openid-connect/token An accepted access token contains the Keycloak issuer for its own realm, the organizor-api audience, and the appropriate realm role: { "iss": "https://localhost:8443/realms/tenant-acme", "aud": ["organizor-api"], "realm_access": { "roles": ["tenant-user"] }, "tenant": "acme" } The tenant claim is a client compatibility hint. Test tenant authorization by pairing the token issuer with the header: GET https://localhost:7184/api/auth/whoami Authorization: Bearer <tenant-acme-token> X-Tenant-Slug: acme Changing the header to X-Tenant-Slug: contoso must return 403 Forbidden. A platform organizor-admin token remains the explicit central-support exception.

articles/local-development.html.title: Local Development | Organizor
articles/local-development.html.summary:
Local Development This page is the canonical reference for running Organizor locally. Use it to confirm the expected ports, startup order, and how the Blazor portal, Keycloak, API, and databases fit together. Note Keep this page as the source of truth for local ports and startup order. Link here from other articles instead of duplicating endpoint tables. Local Topology flowchart LR Browser["Browser"] Portal["Portal UI
https://localhost:7025"] Tvdk["TVDK Website
https://localhost:7122"] Keycloak["Keycloak
https://localhost:8443"] Api["Organizor API
https://localhost:7184"] CatalogDb["Catalog PostgreSQL"] TenantDb["Tenant PostgreSQL databases"] KeycloakDb["Keycloak PostgreSQL
Docker service"] Browser --> Portal Browser --> Tvdk Portal -->|OIDC login| Keycloak Portal -->|Bearer token API calls| Api Tvdk -->|OIDC login| Keycloak Tvdk -->|Bearer token API calls| Api Api -->|JWT issuer metadata| Keycloak Api --> CatalogDb Api --> TenantDb Keycloak --> KeycloakDb Ports And URLs Component URL Notes Platform Portal UI https://localhost:7025 Blazor WebAssembly control-plane HTTPS launch profile. TVDK tenant-admin Portal UI https://localhost:7022 Blazor WebAssembly tenant HTTPS launch profile. Portal UI HTTP http://localhost:5080 Development fallback profile. Prefer HTTPS for auth testing. TVDK website https://localhost:7122 Separate tenant website HTTPS launch profile. TVDK website HTTP http://localhost:5085 Development fallback profile. Prefer HTTPS for auth testing. Organizor API https://localhost:7184 API HTTPS launch profile used by the portal. Organizor API HTTP http://localhost:5100 Useful for direct local API calls without the portal. Keycloak https://localhost:8443 Docker Compose service with local HTTPS certificate. Platform realm issuer https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev Used by the central platform portal. Tenant realm issuer https://localhost:8443/realms/tenant-{slug} Created by tenant onboarding and returned by public auth discovery. Platform token endpoint https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev/protocol/openid-connect/token Used for platform-token testing. Required Local Configuration Copy .env.example to .env and fill the local Keycloak container credentials before running Docker Compose. Keep .env untracked.
