If your .env predates tenant realm isolation, add the new ORGANIZOR_KEYCLOAK_PROVISIONER_CLIENT_ID and ORGANIZOR_KEYCLOAK_PROVISIONER_CLIENT_SECRET entries from .env.example; existing .env files are not updated automatically. The API needs: a ConnectionStrings:Catalog connection string; Postgres settings for tenant database creation and resolution; Keycloak:BaseUrl set to https://localhost:8443; Keycloak:PlatformRealm set to organizor-dev; optionally Keycloak:AdminRealm set explicitly to master (it defaults to master); Keycloak:AdminClientId set to organizor-provisioner; Keycloak:AdminClientSecret from the local provisioner settings in .env. optionally Keycloak:DefaultTenantAdminTemporaryPassword for predictable local-only tenant admin testing; omit it to generate a random temporary password. A newly created default tenant-admin credential is shown only in the successful portal onboarding notice, so copy it before dismissing the notice. Keycloak:DevelopmentAdmin:Username and Keycloak:DevelopmentAdmin:Email for the local platform admin identity. Keycloak:DevelopmentAdmin:Password when you want API startup to seed the local platform admin with the organizor-admin role. Warning The API accepts only its configured platform issuer and active catalog tenant issuers. A tenant token must be issued by the realm owned by the tenant in X-Tenant-Slug. At https://localhost:7025, the Portal is configured to: use Keycloak authority https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev; use Keycloak client ID organizor-ui; redirect login callbacks to https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback; call the API at https://localhost:7184. At a tenant portal host such as https://localhost:7022, the same Portal first resolves GET /api/public/tenant-portals/auth?baseUrl=https%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A7022, validates the returned host/callback/origin values, and then uses the resolved tenant realm and tenant-tvdk-portal client. Portal:PlatformBaseUrl identifies the one fixed platform host. These portal values live in Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui/wwwroot/appsettings.json for local development and must be replaced with deployment URLs for server environments. The separate TVDK tenant website must discover its authority and client id from GET /api/public/tenants/tvdk/auth, then send X-Tenant-Slug: tvdk on authenticated API calls. Its former static shared-realm configuration needs that coordinated update before it is used with this identity model. Startup Order Generate or verify the Keycloak HTTPS certificate at keycloak/certs/keycloak.p12. Start Keycloak with Docker Compose. On an empty Keycloak database, Docker Compose imports docker/keycloak/import/organizor-dev-realm.json and creates the platform realm, clients, roles, and local platform admin user. Run pwsh ./scripts/bootstrap-keycloak-provisioner.ps1 -SkipCertificateCheck to create the master-realm backend provisioner. The switch is restricted to the local loopback Keycloak URL; omit it when the local certificate is trusted by PowerShell. Start the API with the HTTPS launch profile. Start the portal with the HTTPS launch profile. Sign in through the platform portal, onboard a tenant, and verify its public auth contract returns a tenant-specific authority. Commands Start Keycloak: Copy-Item .\.env.example .\.env docker compose --env-file .\.env up -d Run Docker Compose commands from the repository root. From the docs folder, use: docker compose --project-directory .. --env-file ..\.env up -d Reset local Keycloak identity data only when you intentionally want a fresh realm import. This does not delete the API catalog database or tenant PostgreSQL databases: docker compose --env-file .\.env down -v docker compose --env-file .\.env up -d From the docs folder: docker compose --project-directory .. --env-file ..\.env down -v docker compose --project-directory .. --env-file ..\.env up -d docker compose down -v deletes the local Keycloak database volume. The next startup imports docker/keycloak/import/organizor-dev-realm.json again. Run the provisioner bootstrap script after every Keycloak-only reset, then configure API user secrets: dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:BaseUrl" "https://localhost:8443" --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:PlatformRealm" "organizor-dev" --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:AdminRealm" "master" --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:AdminClientId" "organizor-provisioner" --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:AdminClientSecret" "<value from .env>" --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:DevelopmentAdmin:Username" "admin@organizor.dev" --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:DevelopmentAdmin:Email" "admin@organizor.dev" --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:DevelopmentAdmin:Password" "<local-only-password>" --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj The development admin seeder creates the configured platform admin when missing and assigns the organizor-admin role. It does not reset an existing password unless Keycloak:DevelopmentAdmin:ResetPasswordOnStartup is set to true. The realm import also creates admin@organizor.dev with password Admin123! and realm role organizor-admin for local development. If the API starts before Keycloak finishes a fresh import, it logs a warning and continues; restart the API after Keycloak is ready if you need the API seeder to repair the user. Keep Docker Compose values in .env. Keep API development-admin values in user secrets; user secrets are loaded automatically in Development. Full Local Test Reset (Destructive) Use this procedure only for an intentionally disposable local test environment. It permanently deletes all local Keycloak identities, the Organizor catalog, and every local tenant database. It must never be used against shared, staging, or production PostgreSQL servers. Stop the local API and portal so they do not keep PostgreSQL connections open. Type the following confirmation in PowerShell before continuing: $confirmation = Read-Host 'Type RESET-ORGANIZOR-LOCAL to erase local Keycloak, catalog, and tenant data' if ($confirmation -cne 'RESET-ORGANIZOR-LOCAL') { throw 'Full reset cancelled.' } Reset the Keycloak Docker volume: docker compose --env-file .\.env down -v Connect to the local test PostgreSQL server's postgres database with an administrator role from your Postgres/Catalog development configuration. First inventory the exact databases that will be removed: SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'organizor_catalog' OR datname LIKE 'organizor_tenant_%' ORDER BY datname; Verify the result contains only disposable local Organizor databases. Then run one explicit statement for every listed tenant database, followed by the catalog. For example: DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "organizor_tenant_tvdk" WITH (FORCE); DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "organizor_tenant_pjsabbe" WITH (FORCE); DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "organizor_catalog" WITH (FORCE); Do not replace the explicit names with a broad wildcard or run these commands on a non-local server. WITH (FORCE) disconnects local test clients. Start Keycloak again, wait for its health/startup to complete, then bootstrap the provisioner: docker compose --env-file .\.env up -d pwsh ./scripts/bootstrap-keycloak-provisioner.ps1 -SkipCertificateCheck Start the API. It recreates and migrates the empty catalog. Sign in through the platform portal, onboard new test tenants with both their public website and tenant-admin portal URLs, and obtain each tenant website's realm authority from public auth discovery. The API PostgreSQL server is not managed by docker-compose.yml; only the Keycloak PostgreSQL volume is. That is why both the Docker reset and the explicit catalog/tenant database reset are required for a true clean test environment. Run the API: dotnet run --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj --launch-profile https Run the portal: dotnet run --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui\Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui.csproj --launch-profile https Run the tenant-admin portal profile after onboarding TVDK with tenantAdminPortalBaseUrl set to https://localhost:7022: dotnet run --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui\Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui.csproj --launch-profile tenant-https Build the documentation: docfx .\docs\docfx.json Generate a local documentation deploy key only when you need to update the GitHub DOCS_DEPLOY_KEY secret: New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\ssh ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "organizor-docs-deploy" -f .\ssh\organizor-docs-key The private key stays at ssh/organizor-docs-key and ssh/ is gitignored. Do not commit, copy into docs output, or delete this folder unless you are intentionally rotating the deploy key. Store the private key value in the GitHub Actions secret DOCS_DEPLOY_KEY, and add the public key ssh/organizor-docs-key.pub as a deploy key on the public documentation repository. Keycloak Client Requirements The organizor-ui client must allow the portal origin: Setting Value Valid redirect URI https://localhost:7025/* Login callback https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback Web origin https://localhost:7025 After TVDK is onboarded, its realm-local tenant-tvdk-web client must allow the local TVDK origin: Setting Value Valid redirect URI https://localhost:7122/authentication/login-callback Web origin https://localhost:7122 Post-logout redirect URI https://localhost:7122/ If the TVDK sign-in flow shows Invalid parameter: redirect_uri, update the tenant-tvdk-web client in the tenant-tvdk realm with the exact callback URI above. For HTTP-profile testing, also allow http://localhost:5085/authentication/login-callback, http://localhost:5085, and http://localhost:5085/. The TVDK website must still discover its authority and client id from GET /api/public/tenants/tvdk/auth rather than hard-coding the platform realm. The same onboarding also creates tenant-tvdk-portal in tenant-tvdk for the tenant-admin Portal host: Setting Value Valid redirect URI https://localhost:7022/authentication/login-callback Post-logout redirect URI https://localhost:7022 Web origin https://localhost:7022 The portal client is distinct from tenant-tvdk-web; do not merge their redirect/origin settings. The backend-only organizor-provisioner client in the Keycloak master realm performs API service-account operations during tenant onboarding and deletion. pwsh ./scripts/bootstrap-keycloak-provisioner.ps1 -SkipCertificateCheck explicitly maps and scopes its master admin role, then smoke-verifies an Admin REST call without printing its secret or token. The certificate-bypass switch is allowed only for loopback URLs. Keep that client secret only in API configuration or deployment secrets. Production Checklist Do not copy local wildcard origins, local certificates, or development secrets into deployed environments. Production should use real HTTPS certificates, explicit origins, and managed secret storage. Verification Checklist Use this checklist when local authentication or API calls fail: Keycloak opens at https://localhost:8443 without a certificate warning. The API Keycloak:BaseUrl is exactly https://localhost:8443, Keycloak:PlatformRealm is organizor-dev, and the provisioner settings point to master / organizor-provisioner. The portal login callback is allowed by the organizor-ui client. The TVDK login callback is allowed by the tenant-tvdk-web client when testing the separate tenant website. The portal calls https://localhost:7184, not the API HTTP endpoint. The API HTTPS profile is running before logging in through the portal. A platform portal token has organizor-admin from the platform realm and the organizor-api audience. A tenant website token has realm-local tenant roles, the organizor-api audience, and an issuer matching its X-Tenant-Slug; its optional tenant claim is not used as the access boundary. Related Guides Keycloak HTTPS Setup explains certificate generation and browser trust. Keycloak Setup explains realm, client, role, group, and claim mapper configuration. Configuration documents API configuration sections. Portal UI Overview documents the Blazor portal responsibilities and integration points.

articles/localization.html.title: Localization | Organizor
articles/localization.html.summary: Localization Organizor provides multilingual support for error responses using a simple, predictable, API-friendly localization pipeline. Supported Languages Organizor currently supports: en - English (fallback) nl - Dutch Additional languages can be added by creating new resource files in the Code7Dev.Organizor.Api/Resources folder. How Localization Works Localization is driven by the standard Accept-Language HTTP header. Example: Accept-Language: nl The API resolves the culture for the request and uses it to translate error messages. If a translation is missing, the system falls back to English (en). Key Principles Application services return error codes only, such as TENANT_NOT_FOUND. The API middleware maps those codes to localized resource strings. No hardcoded user-facing messages exist in the domain or application layers. Localization is deterministic and client-controlled. Culture Resolution Organizor uses the following resolution order: Accept-Language header. Fallback to English (en). This keeps behavior predictable and client-controlled. Error Code Translation Each error code corresponds to a resource key. Examples: TENANT_NOT_FOUND TENANT_ALREADY_EXISTS UNEXPECTED_ERROR These keys exist in: Code7Dev.Organizor.Api/Resources/Shared.en.resx Code7Dev.Organizor.Api/Resources/Shared.nl.resx The middleware retrieves the localized string and injects it into the RFC 7807 problem response. Example Request and Response Request: GET /api/v1/tenants/unknown Authorization: Bearer <platform-organizor-admin-token> Accept-Language: nl Response: { "type": "https://httpstatuses.com/404", "title": "Tenant niet gevonden", "status": 404, "error": "TENANT_NOT_FOUND", "correlationId": "abc123" } The error code remains stable and language-independent. The title is localized based on the request culture. Adding New Translations To add a new language: Create a new .resx file, for example Shared.fr.resx. Add the same error keys as in the English file. Provide translated values. Register the culture in AddApiLocalization. Restart the API.

articles/portal-admin-workflows.html.title: Portal Admin Workflows | Organizor
articles/portal-admin-workflows.html.summary: Portal Admin Workflows Platform administration routes use AdminLayout and require organizor-admin issued by the configured platform realm. The admin shell groups navigation into Overview and Platform sections, with /admin/users intentionally remaining a tenant-row deep link rather than a standalone sidebar item. A platform administrator has one control-plane login; the backend provisioner manages separate tenant realms without giving the administrator tenant or master credentials. Dashboard The /admin dashboard is a read-only platform overview. It loads tenant and plan data through AdminTenantService, summarizes tenant lifecycle state, highlights failed tenant records, shows active and inactive plan counts, and links to tenant and plan management. The dashboard does not add new API endpoints or mutate tenant data. Tenant Management The admin tenant page uses Radzen components and the AdminTenantService client. It supports: loading all tenants including soft-deleted tenants; filtering tenants by name, slug, database name, or status; viewing active, deleted, and failed tenant counts; onboarding a tenant with website and auth metadata; upgrading a tenant database by running pending migrations; soft-deleting a tenant with an operator reason; hard-deleting a previously soft-deleted tenant; opening user management for active tenants; inspecting effective tenant config; editing tenant plan assignment and tenant-level overrides. inspecting a tenant's entitled and installed modules; installing an optional add-on, retrying a failed or interrupted installation, or enabling/disabling an installed module without deleting its business data. UI action API endpoint Load tenants GET /api/admin/tenants Load one tenant GET /api/admin/tenants/{id} Onboard tenant POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard Upgrade tenant POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/upgrade Inspect effective config GET /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config Load tenant overrides GET /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config-overrides Save tenant overrides PUT /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config-overrides Inspect tenant modules GET /api/admin/tenants/{id}/modules Install tenant module POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/modules/{moduleKey}/install Retry failed or interrupted module installation POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/modules/{moduleKey}/retry Enable tenant module POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/modules/{moduleKey}/enable Disable tenant module POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/modules/{moduleKey}/disable Soft delete tenant DELETE /api/admin/tenants/{id} Hard delete tenant POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/hard-delete Tenant onboarding stores website/auth settings in centralized tenant config, assigns immutable IdentityRealm tenant-{slug}, and provisions that realm so tenant website auth can use Organizor as the source of truth. The onboarding dialog also selects an active plan; successful onboarding automatically installs that plan's included modules. Soft delete disables the tenant realm before catalog deletion state is recorded. Hard delete removes the complete tenant realm before database and catalog cleanup. An identity-provider failure stops the destructive action and is surfaced as TENANT_IDENTITY_PROVIDER_FAILED. The tenant drawer separates Modules from legacy configuration. Its module section shows plan availability, installation state, source, dependency readiness, and any failure reason. A disabled module retains data, and a module with an enabled dependent cannot be disabled. Plan Management The admin plans page uses AdminTenantService and supports loading and editing tenant plan definitions. Its Modules tab manages the plan's product bundle separately from legacy feature and settings defaults. UI action API endpoint Load plans GET /api/admin/tenant-plans Save plan defaults PUT /api/admin/tenant-plans/{planKey} Load deployed module catalog GET /api/admin/modules Load plan module entitlements GET /api/admin/tenant-plans/{planKey}/module-entitlements Save plan module entitlements PUT /api/admin/tenant-plans/{planKey}/module-entitlements Plan keys are intentionally immutable. The entitlement editor assigns every deployed module one of Included, Optional add-on, or Unavailable. An included module is installed at successful onboarding; an optional module needs an explicit tenant action. See Tenant Modules for the lifecycle constraints. Tenant User Control Plane The tenant catalog page is the entry point for platform tenant-user management. Platform administrators open users from an active tenant row, which navigates to /admin/users?tenantId={id}. The admin users page manages only that tenant's realm-local Keycloak users. It can create users, list users, toggle enabled state, delete users, and assign tenant roles within the selected tenant. The same username may exist in another tenant realm without being the same identity. The admin sidebar does not expose /admin/users as a standalone global directory. /admin/users without a valid active tenant id redirects to /admin/tenants.

articles/portal-overview.html.title: Portal UI Overview | Organizor
articles/portal-overview.html.summary: Portal UI Overview The Portal UI is the Blazor WebAssembly front end for Organizor platform and tenant administration. It handles platform-realm Keycloak sign-in at the control-plane host, tenant-realm Keycloak sign-in at a tenant portal host, public registration testing, and authenticated API calls to the backend. The Portal is deliberately not a shared-realm tenant login. It selects a mode once at startup from its actual host: Portal:PlatformBaseUrl uses static platform OIDC configuration, while every other host must resolve an exact tenant portal runtime contract before it starts OIDC. Current Capabilities Area Details Platform administration Portal Admin Workflows Tenant administration Portal Tenant Workflows through the tenant-specific portal host and realm-local OIDC client. Authentication Authentication Flow API clients API Integration Route and component structure UI Structure Technology Stack Blazor WebAssembly for client-side rendering. .NET 10 for the portal project. Keycloak for authentication using OIDC Authorization Code Flow with PKCE. Radzen.Blazor for the admin tenant grid, cards, forms, buttons, badges, alerts, and notifications. IHttpClientFactory plus a custom AuthorizationMessageHandler for API calls. Routes and Layouts AdminLayout groups platform navigation into Overview and Platform sections. TenantLayout is served only through the matching tenant portal host after tenant-realm sign-in; the control-plane host does not route tenant administrators into it. Route Layout Required role Purpose / MainLayout none Entry page. Authenticated users are redirected by role. /admin AdminLayout organizor-admin Platform dashboard for tenant lifecycle, plan library, and catalog health. /admin/tenants AdminLayout organizor-admin Tenant catalog and lifecycle management. /admin/plans AdminLayout organizor-admin Tenant plan default management. /admin/users?tenantId={id} AdminLayout organizor-admin Platform control-plane user management for one active tenant. /tenant TenantLayout matching tenant realm tenant-admin Tenant dashboard. /tenant/users TenantLayout matching tenant realm tenant-admin Tenant user management. /tenant/people TenantLayout matching tenant realm tenant-admin Tenant people and family administration. /tenant/organizations TenantLayout matching tenant realm tenant-admin Tenant organization management. /tenant/activities TenantLayout matching tenant realm tenant-admin Tenant activity setup. /tenant/registrations TenantLayout matching tenant realm tenant-admin Tenant registration management. /tenant/config TenantLayout matching tenant realm tenant-admin Tenant configuration. /tenant/profile TenantLayout matching tenant realm tenant-admin Tenant administrator profile. /access-denied MainLayout authenticated user Fallback page for authenticated users without portal roles. /register PublicLayout none Temporary public tenant-user self-registration shell. /logout none authenticated user Redirects to the Blazor OIDC logout endpoint and returns to /. /authentication/* authentication page none Blazor WebAssembly OIDC endpoints. RoleRedirector is mounted globally in App.razor, but it only redirects from neutral entry routes (/ and the login callback). In platform mode it sends only a platform-realm organizor-admin to /admin. In tenant mode it verifies the tenant claim and issuer match the resolved portal tenant, then sends a tenant-admin to /tenant; a regular tenant user goes to the configured public website. It must not redirect when the user is already on a target area, otherwise the portal can reload-loop. Public Registration Shell The /register page is a temporary public shell for exercising tenant-user self-registration. It posts to POST /api/public/register through PublicRegistrationService. The long-term model is that tenant-specific static websites own their registration UI and call the public API contract directly. Participant-facing activity registration forms are not backend portal pages. This keeps tenant branding and UX independent from the Organizor portal. Tenant rows expose the catalog and lifecycle fields used by the UI: Field Use id Action target for upgrade and delete calls. name, slug, databaseName Catalog display and search. createdAt Created timestamp shown in local time. status Lifecycle state used for badges and failed counts. failureReason Failure detail shown below the tenant name when present. isDeleted Controls deleted badge state and whether hard delete is available. Summary The supported portal surface is the platform dashboard, tenant lifecycle operations, tenant plan defaults, tenant-level config overrides, platform tenant-user management, and public registration testing at the control-plane host; and tenant business administration at a matching tenant portal host. Regular tenant-user profile, family, and registration workflows belong in tenant-specific public UIs such as TVDK.

articles/portal-tenant-workflows.html.title: Portal Tenant Workflows | Organizor
articles/portal-tenant-workflows.html.summary: Portal Tenant Workflows Tenant business APIs require a token from the resolved tenant's own Keycloak realm, the realm-local tenant-admin role, and X-Tenant-Slug where the route is tenant-scoped. The API validates issuer-to-tenant binding; a tenant claim or group path is not that boundary. The central Portal host is configured only for the platform realm. The same Portal application serves TenantLayout through a tenant's configured portal host, which resolves a tenant-specific runtime OIDC contract before sign-in. Unless a section explicitly says Platform Administration, the workflows below describe that supported tenant-local portal surface and its tenant API contracts. Tenant boundary: a tenant portal sends its resolved X-Tenant-Slug for tenant-scoped API calls, but the API authorizes it by the token issuer mapped to the catalog tenant. The old shared-realm automatic-header model must not be used. The tenant shell groups navigation into Overview, Operations, Directory, and Settings sections. Operations contains activity setup and registration review. Directory contains families and people, organizations, and users. Settings contains tenant configuration and the tenant-admin profile. Shared List And Detail Pattern Tenant-admin list pages are list-first: the directory or grid remains readable while selecting a record opens a right-side off-canvas drawer. Selected-record editing and related workflows stay inside that drawer rather than stacking another modal over it. A focused page-level create modal remains appropriate when no record has been selected. When a list row has several secondary actions, the portal groups them in a text-labelled three-dot overflow menu. Activity setup demonstrates both parts of this pattern. People demonstrates the drawer workflow; its current directory has no secondary row actions that need an overflow menu. When a list page has four summary metrics, it uses the shared horizontal icon KPI bar. The bar collapses responsively instead of presenting four separate metric cards. Platform Administration Platform administrators use /admin as the operational overview for tenant lifecycle, plan availability, catalog health, and recent tenant records. Its four summary metrics use the same horizontal icon KPI bar as the tenant-admin surfaces. /admin/tenants is list-first: the catalog stays full-width for scanning and filtering, onboarding opens in a focused page-level modal, and selecting a tenant opens a right-side detail drawer. The drawer retains the existing effective configuration view, tenant overrides, upgrade, tenant-user navigation, and lifecycle actions. Secondary row actions are grouped in the existing three-dot action menu; soft and hard deletion keep explicit confirmations. /admin/plans keeps plan defaults in the existing tabbed editor and makes the configuration order explicit: system defaults, plan defaults, then optional tenant overrides. /admin/users?tenantId={id} remains scoped to one active tenant and uses the same KPI, create-modal, and selected-user drawer pattern; it is not a global user directory. Dashboard The /tenant dashboard is a read-only operational overview for tenant admins. It summarizes activity state, upcoming activities, tracked registrations, payment follow-up, capacity usage, people, and active organizations. The dashboard uses a compact KPI bar, action bar, and tab-style sections for overview, launch readiness, and activity operations. The overview keeps needs-attention as the primary panel, with upcoming activities and recent registrations beside it. The dashboard also shows tenant context, local verification status, last refreshed time, and remembers the last selected tab in browser storage. During first load it shows skeleton placeholders, and when the Organizor API is unreachable it shows one connection state instead of misleading zero metrics. If the tenant public website URL is discoverable from the public auth contract, the action bar includes a public-site link. The launch readiness checklist groups checks into tenant setup, activity setup, registration setup, communication, and parent access. It checks whether the tenant has basic configuration, SMTP settings, activity types, active upcoming activities, registration setup, public activity page content, validation rules, confirmation templates, and parent-managed registration prerequisites. Repeated dashboard rows use small reusable components for consistency. The checklist links each item to the existing management page and is operational guidance only; it is not a persisted launch approval. The first dashboard slice reuses existing tenant-scoped portal services. Registration metrics are loaded through bounded per-activity calls for current and upcoming activities, so very large tenants may see a scoped summary until a dedicated aggregation API is accepted. If one dashboard source is unavailable, the page renders available sections and shows a partial-data warning. Tenant User Management Tenant administrators can open /tenant/users to manage users for their own tenant. The shared horizontal icon KPI row summarizes total, enabled, tenant-admin, and required-action counts. The page is list-first: it supports client-side search across loaded users, visibly distinguishes roles, sign-in state, and required identity-provider actions, and opens a selected user in a right-side drawer. Create user opens in a focused modal with identity, sign-in setup, and tenant-access sections. The selected-user drawer keeps enable/disable, role-change, and removal actions close to the record they affect. Removal disables the user's realm-local identity and removes its realm-local role memberships; it cannot delete or disable any identity in another tenant realm. Platform administrators use the same interaction pattern from /admin/users?tenantId={id}, where the selected active tenant remains visible as the scope. Regular tenant-user accounts do not see either management route. People Tenant administrators can open /tenant/people to create and edit tenant-local people and manage directional relationships between them. Relationship direction is from the responsible/contact person to the child or related person. The page is directory-first. The default Directory tab is the complete canonical list of people. A separate Family tab shows current active family links while keeping each person on one row: responsible adults and contacts, people they manage, relationship type, primary-contact, communication, and registration-management signals remain together. This avoids duplicating a participant under several adults or implying ownership. People with no active family link remain visible in both views. Selecting a row or a linked-person name opens the existing off-canvas right-side detail drawer. The Family tab loads its people and active relationship links from the tenant-admin GET /api/v1/people/family-directory snapshot. It replaces the previous one-relationship-request-per-person summary preload. Inactive and archived relationship history remains in the selected person's drawer management workflow rather than being presented as a current family connection. The drawer has overview, relationship, management, and detail tabs for portal login state, responsible adults, managed children, and relationship flags for primary contact, registration management, and communication receipt. Page-level person creation uses a focused modal. Selected-person edit, portal login connect/disconnect, and relationship editing stay inside the drawer as workflow modes so admins do not stack competing overlays. The people page also lets tenant administrators connect or disconnect the selected person from an existing tenant user login. Parent-managed registration resolves the signed-in parent or guardian through this user-person link. The page exposes relationship flags for primary contact, registration management, and communication receipt. Only one active primary-contact relationship can exist for a child. Duplicate active relationships with the same source person, target person, and relationship type are rejected. Parent-Managed Registration Parent-managed registration is not a portal workflow. Regular tenant users use tenant-specific public UIs such as TVDK for profile, family dashboard, managed-child registration, and child registration cancellation. Those clients use tenant-user read-only activity endpoints under /api/v1/me instead of tenant-admin activity setup endpoints. The child-registration request submits the child person id plus the activity-specific field payload to the backend. The backend enforces the same validation rules used by public registration and rejects unmanaged child selection. Organizations Tenant administrators can open /tenant/organizations to list, create, and edit tenant-local organizations. The shared horizontal icon KPI row summarizes total, active, inactive, and archived records. The directory remains full-width while text, type, and status filters help distinguish those records; archived records remain visible by default. Selecting an organization opens a right-side overview/edit drawer, while page-level creation opens a focused modal. The portal exposes name, type, status, contact fields, optional KBO number and bank account, and structured address fields. The edit workflow groups identity, contact, address, and administrative details. New organization forms default country to Belgium and create organizations as active. Status changes use the existing update workflow and stay with the selected organization. Activity Setup Tenant administrators can open /tenant/activities to manage tenant-local activity setup. The page has Activity Types and Activities tabs. The activity type tab supports list, create, edit, activate, and deactivate actions. Create and edit open in a right-side off-canvas editor so the configured activity type list stays full-width. Tenant admins can configure registration field definitions, enable fiscal or healthcare document capabilities on existing activity types, and configure default registration confirmation email templates. The activities tab supports list, create, edit, activate, and deactivate actions. Create and edit open in a right-side off-canvas editor so the configured activity list stays full-width. Activities can reference an activity type and optionally a tenant-local organization. Existing activities can define a registration confirmation email override or delete that override to fall back to the activity type default. Secondary activity type and activity row actions are grouped in a three-dot menu; selecting the row opens the drawer, so the list does not duplicate Edit as a visible row action. The public activity page editor can start from the backend-provided standard activity page template. Applying the template replaces the activity public detail content with an editable copy; tenant admins can then adjust the hero, reorder blocks, or add/remove sections for that activity. The editor also exposes explicit quick-add controls for the TVDK-rendered sections: practical information, day schedule, FAQ, testimonial, and gallery. Registration confirmation templates open in a dedicated reusable mail-template editor page from the activity type and activity rows. The activity setup drawers do not duplicate those template fields. The editor uses a WYSIWYG HTML body field, plain-text body, subject, recipient mode, culture, enable flag, sender name override, and reply-to email. Registration validation rules now open in a dedicated reusable editor page from the activity type and activity rows. The page is scope-based and concise: it edits backend-enforced rules for the current activity type or activity, shows the effective rule set, and keeps the rule catalog limited to the supported core targets. For regex rules, the editor offers preset helpers for common formats such as digits-only and email-like values, while still allowing a custom pattern when needed. Registration Management Tenant administrators can open /tenant/registrations to review registrations for a selected activity. The default queue leads with submitted registrations needing a status decision. Separate queue filters expose payment follow-up (non-cancelled unpaid or pending registrations), confirmed registrations, cancelled registrations, or the complete activity list. Status, payment state, participant, payment reference, and registration id filters remain activity-scoped so the selected activity context stays visible. The page is list-first. Selecting a registration opens an off-canvas right-side drawer with overview, submitted core data, custom field values, status and manual-payment actions, payment metadata, available audit timestamps, and document actions. Tenant admins can confirm or cancel registrations. They can also mark non-cancelled registrations as paid with an optional payment reference, or mark them unpaid. Cancelled registrations reject later confirmation and payment updates. Low-frequency document actions are also available through a text-labelled three-dot overflow menu in the list. Fiscal and healthcare attestation downloads return PDF files. Send actions use tenant SMTP settings to email the generated PDF to the parent or guardian email when the selected registration, activity type capability, activity, person, relationship, and organization data are eligible. Public participant registration submission is API-only in this slice through POST /api/v1/activities/{activityId}/public-registrations. Registration confirmation preview, test-send, resend, and delivery history are exposed through backend tenant-admin APIs. Dedicated portal controls for those registration-level actions are deferred. Tenant Config Tenant admins can open /tenant/config. The page calls GET /api/v1/tenant/config through TenantConfigService. The default view is operational: it summarizes the resolved plan, enabled feature flags, registration behavior, public website/auth readiness, and SMTP readiness. Tenant mail setup and test delivery remain editable through the existing tenant settings endpoints. Raw effective settings JSON is available from the Diagnostics tab for troubleshooting. Regular tenant-user accounts should not see tenant configuration in the portal. Tenant Profile Tenant admins can open /tenant/profile. A persistent signed-in account summary keeps display name, email, resolved tenant, and access context visible. Profile, Security, and Diagnostics tabs separate routine name updates, Keycloak-backed account actions, and troubleshooting claims. The Profile tab uses PUT /api/v1/tenant/account-actions/profile to update only Keycloak firstName and lastName; all other identity fields remain read-only. The Security tab explains that Keycloak owns credentials, makes password change available through POST /api/v1/tenant/account-actions/change-password, and keeps unavailable future security controls visibly disabled. The portal does not collect new passwords and does not expose a direct Keycloak account-console link. Tenant website return navigation remains in the shell account panel. Regular tenant users use tenant-specific public UIs for their own profile and account-action UX. These self-service actions operate only on the caller's own realm-local identity; platform support uses /api/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/users for another user's management.

articles/public-website-api.html.title: Public Website API | Organizor
articles/public-website-api.html.summary: Public Website API Public website endpoints are anonymous by design. They return non-secret tenant auth metadata, public activity registration metadata, or create tenant/user-facing records through explicitly public contracts. Public Activity Registration Discovery Tenant public websites can list active anonymous-registerable activity-type segments for navigation, list activities for their configured tenant, and load a direct registration form by activity id. These discovery endpoints require X-Tenant-Slug because they read tenant-scoped activity data from the resolved tenant database. GET /api/v1/public/activity-types X-Tenant-Slug: acme Accept: application/json Returns active anonymous-registerable activity types that have at least one active public activity. Tenant websites can use this response for segment navigation such as a sidebar. GET /api/v1/public/activities X-Tenant-Slug: acme Accept: application/json Returns active activities whose activity type is active and uses anonymous registration mode. Each item includes the activity GUID, activity type metadata, display fields, price, image URL when configured, and registration availability. Use GET /api/v1/public/activities?activityTypeKey=swimming to list only one activity-type segment. GET /api/v1/public/activities/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/registration-form X-Tenant-Slug: acme Accept: application/json Returns the same public activity display data plus active registration fields. Field options are returned as public option objects with value and label. The first-slice availability values are open and full. Public websites submit the completed form through the existing endpoint: POST /api/v1/activities/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/public-registrations X-Tenant-Slug: acme Content-Type: application/json Status Meaning 200 OK Public activity metadata or registration form metadata returned. 400 Bad Request Tenant slug is missing/invalid, the activity is inactive, or the activity is not publicly registerable. 404 Not Found Activity or activity type was not found for the resolved tenant. 500 Internal Server Error Unexpected server error. See Errors and Observability. Static Tenant Website Auth Contract GET /api/public/tenants/acme/auth Accept: application/json Returns the public OIDC settings a tenant-specific website needs before login. The endpoint returns data only for active, non-deleted tenants. Example response: { "tenantSlug": "acme", "authority": "https://localhost:8443/realms/tenant-acme", "clientId": "tenant-acme-web", "websiteBaseUrl": "https://acme.example.com", "responseType": "code", "usePkce": true, "tenantHeaderName": "X-Tenant-Slug", "tenantClaimName": "tenant", "tenantUserRole": "tenant-user", "tenantAdminRole": "tenant-admin", "tenantUserGroupPath": "/users", "tenantAdminGroupPath": "/admins", "scopes": ["openid", "profile", "email"], "loginRedirectUris": ["https://acme.example.com/authentication/login-callback"], "logoutRedirectUris": ["https://acme.example.com"], "webOrigins": ["https://acme.example.com"], "registrationRedirectUrl": "https://acme.example.com/register/complete", "publicRegistrationEndpoint": "/api/public/register" } The authority is the catalog tenant's own Keycloak realm. A PJsabbe website receives tenant-pjsabbe; a TVDK website receives tenant-tvdk. Do not replace that authority with the platform realm or hard-code a shared realm in a tenant website. Static tenant websites use this contract during startup to configure OIDC Authorization Code Flow with PKCE, select the generated tenant client id, request openid profile email, and send X-Tenant-Slug on authenticated tenant-scoped API calls after login. They derive callback and logout URLs from their own deployed base URL and must verify those URLs and their browser origin appear in the contract before they start login. A mismatch is an onboarding/deployment configuration problem; never fall back to the platform authority or client. Tenant website tokens contain realm-local tenant-user or tenant-admin roles and an organizor-api audience. They may also contain tenant: acme for client compatibility, but the API authorizes using the issuer-to-tenant binding, not that claim or the group-path strings. Status Meaning 200 OK Contract returned for an active tenant. 400 Bad Request Tenant slug or stored auth settings are invalid. 404 Not Found Tenant does not exist, is deleted, or is not active. Tenant-Admin Portal Auth Contract GET /api/public/tenant-portals/auth?baseUrl=https%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A7022 Accept: application/json This anonymous endpoint exists so the Portal can configure OIDC before a tenant administrator signs in. It normalizes the supplied base URL, resolves exactly one active tenant by its catalog-owned AdminPortalBaseUrl, and returns only public client metadata. { "tenantSlug": "tvdk", "authority": "https://localhost:8443/realms/tenant-tvdk", "clientId": "tenant-tvdk-portal", "websiteBaseUrl": "https://localhost:7122", "responseType": "code", "usePkce": true, "scopes": ["openid", "profile", "email"], "loginRedirectUri": "https://localhost:7022/authentication/login-callback", "logoutRedirectUri": "https://localhost:7022", "webOrigin": "https://localhost:7022" } The Portal validates its actual base URL, callback URL, logout URL, and origin against this contract before starting OIDC. An unknown or inactive portal URL returns TENANT_NOT_FOUND; an invalid URL returns TENANT_CONFIG_INVALID. The endpoint never returns a secret, Keycloak administration credential, or platform OIDC configuration. Public Tenant User Registration POST /api/public/register Content-Type: application/json { "tenantSlug": "acme", "username": "jane.doe", "email": "jane@example.com", "password": "correct-horse-battery-staple" } Creates an enabled tenant-user account for an active tenant. This endpoint does not use X-Tenant-Slug; the tenant is selected from the request body. Registration creates the identity in the tenant's own Keycloak realm and assigns it to realm-local /users. The API validates that the tenant exists, is active, has effective settings.registration.enabled set to boolean true, and has not reached its configured user limit. Username and email uniqueness are evaluated inside that realm, so the same login name can exist independently in another tenant realm. The portal /register page is a temporary shell for testing this feature. Tenant-specific websites should provide their own UI and call this API contract directly. Tenant administrators use their tenant-specific Portal host rather than the public website client. Status Meaning 200 OK User was created and assigned to the realm-local tenant-user group. 400 Bad Request Request validation failed, effective registration config is invalid, or registration is disabled. 404 Not Found Tenant slug does not resolve to an active tenant. 409 Conflict Username or email already exists in that tenant realm, or the tenant user limit was reached. 502 Bad Gateway Keycloak rejected the user operation or could not complete it. 500 Internal Server Error Unexpected server error. See Errors and Observability.

articles/role-based-authorization.html.title: Role-Based Authorization | Organizor
articles/role-based-authorization.html.summary: Role-Based Authorization Overview The API authorizes requests with issuer-aware ASP.NET Core policies backed by Keycloak realm roles. Authentication validates the JWT first, tenant access middleware binds a tenant-scoped request to its catalog-owned realm, and endpoint authorization policies apply the issuer-appropriate role rule. A role string alone never grants access. The realm that issued it matters. Realm Roles Role Owning realm Purpose organizor-admin Platform realm only Platform administrator. Manages catalog tenants and control-plane operations. tenant-admin Tenant realm only Tenant administrator. Uses tenant-aware application endpoints for that realm. tenant-user Tenant realm only Tenant member. Uses shared tenant-aware application endpoints for that realm. Tenant realms contain no platform administrator identities. A tenant realm role named organizor-admin cannot grant control-plane access. JWT Trust And Role Sources The API accepts a JWT only when all of the following are true: its issuer is the configured platform realm or an active catalog tenant realm; its signature, expiry, and issuer are valid; it contains aud: organizor-api. OpenID metadata and signing keys are fetched only after the issuer passes the allow-list. The API maps roles from Keycloak realm_access.roles to ASP.NET Core ClaimTypes.Role: { "iss": "https://localhost:8443/realms/tenant-acme", "aud": ["organizor-api"], "realm_access": { "roles": ["tenant-user"] } } Client roles from arbitrary Keycloak clients are not the authorization source for Organizor policies. Tenant website clients are configured to emit the required realm roles and API audience. Policies Policy Accepted issuer and role RequireOrganizorAdminRole Platform issuer with organizor-admin only. RequireTenantUserRole Matching tenant issuer with tenant-admin or tenant-user; a platform organizor-admin is the centralized-support exception. RequireTenantAdminRole Matching tenant issuer with tenant-admin; a platform organizor-admin is the centralized-support exception. Use policies for new endpoints unless the endpoint is intentionally authentication-only. [Authorize(Policy = AuthorizationPolicies.RequireOrganizorAdminRole)] Current Endpoint Enforcement Endpoint area Policy /api/admin/tenants/* RequireOrganizorAdminRole /api/admin/tenant-plans/* RequireOrganizorAdminRole POST /api/v1/tenants RequireOrganizorAdminRole GET /api/v1/tenants RequireOrganizorAdminRole GET /api/v1/tenants/{slug} RequireOrganizorAdminRole GET /api/v1/tenant/config RequireTenantAdminRole POST /api/public/register anonymous GET /api/auth/whoami authenticated user only Tenant Interaction Role checks do not replace tenant checks. For tenant-scoped routes, a user must pass both: issuer-to-tenant authorization in TenantAccessMiddleware; endpoint role or policy authorization in ASP.NET Core. This means a tenant-acme token is denied when it sends X-Tenant-Slug: contoso, even when its role is otherwise valid. The tenant claim is a compatibility hint, not evidence of membership. The old behavior that treated a token with no tenant claim as a platform superadmin is removed. Managing Roles Platform administrators use the Organizor portal/API with their normal platform login. Tenant users and roles are managed through the selected tenant's Organizor administration endpoints, which target that tenant's catalog-owned realm. The backend organizor-provisioner service account performs Keycloak Admin REST work; its secret and the Keycloak master realm are never browser or tenant administrator credentials. For local diagnosis, inspect the correct realm in Keycloak: organizor-dev contains platform organizor-admin identities; tenant-{slug} contains that tenant's tenant-admin and tenant-user identities. Do not use a Keycloak console role assignment as the normal production workflow, because it bypasses Organizor's application-level user management and audit path. Test Matrix Scenario Expected Platform organizor-admin calls /api/admin/tenants Allowed Tenant tenant-user calls /api/admin/tenants 403 Forbidden Tenant tenant-admin calls GET /api/v1/tenants 403 Forbidden Tenant tenant-user calls GET /api/v1/tenants 403 Forbidden Tenant tenant-user calls GET /api/v1/tenant/config for their tenant 403 Forbidden Tenant tenant-user from tenant-acme calls a contoso tenant route 403 Forbidden Tenant realm role named organizor-admin calls a platform route 403 Forbidden Platform organizor-admin supports a selected active tenant Allowed where the endpoint policy permits it Token from a soft-deleted tenant realm 401 Unauthorized Anonymous user calls POST /api/public/register for an active tenant with registration enabled Allowed

articles/security.html.title: Security | Organizor
articles/security.html.summary: Security CORS Development CORS allows any origin, method, and header. Production CORS currently uses ProdCors, but no production origins are configured in code. Add explicit origins before relying on browser clients in production. Internal Admin Routes Routes under /api/admin/tenants and /api/admin/tenant-plans are internal operations routes. They perform provisioning, upgrades, soft deletion, hard deletion, effective-config reads, tenant override edits, and plan default edits. These endpoints require the RequireOrganizorAdminRole policy. Only tokens with the organizor-admin role can call them. Config override and plan default edits should be treated as privileged changes. They can affect tenant-visible limits and feature availability without changing tenant database data. Error Detail Unhandled exceptions currently include ex.Message in problem details. This is useful for internal development and AI-assisted debugging, but it may expose sensitive implementation details in production. Tenant Resolution Tenant-scoped routes depend on X-Tenant-Slug. GET /api/v1/tenant/config is tenant-scoped, requires a tenant-admin role, and returns the effective config for the current tenant. Platform routes such as /api/v1/tenants, /api/admin, /health, /openapi, and /scalar skip tenant resolution. Destructive Operations Hard deletion drops the tenant database. The service requires a tenant to be soft-deleted before hard deletion, which protects active tenants from immediate physical removal.

articles/spec-driven-development.html.title: Spec-Driven Development | Organizor
articles/spec-driven-development.html.summary: Spec-Driven Development Organizor uses Spec-Driven Development for feature work. Accepted behavior is stored in repository specifications under spec/ so requirements, implementation, tests, and documentation are versioned with the code. Constitution Before feature work starts, read: brief.md tech-design.md roadmap.md rules.md workflow.md AGENTS.md the relevant feature files under spec/features/ These files define customer intent, architecture boundaries, implementation constraints, feature order, standing rules, workflow, and agent behavior. Feature Specs Each feature lives in spec/features/{feature-slug}/ and contains: File Purpose specification.md Defines behavior, scope, authorization, tenancy, persistence, API impact, acceptance criteria, and open questions. implementation.md Maps the spec to projects, layers, migrations, and rollback considerations. testing.md Defines automated and manual verification. documentation.md Defines DocFX, README, operator, and integration documentation updates. finalise.md Records completion checklist, verification results, residual risk, and follow-up work. Use spec/_templates/feature/ when starting a feature. Feature Discovery And Health New and newly touched feature specifications add a lightweight discovery block directly below Status: Status: accepted Delivery: not-started Area: portal Tags: tenant-admin, registration Next Action: Implement the queue/detail review UI. Depends On: tenant-registration-management Legacy specifications without this block remain valid. The repository tool derives their delivery state from the existing specification, implementation, and finalise status files. After reading the constitution, use the discovery command to find the smallest relevant specification set: pwsh ./scripts/spec.ps1 catalog pwsh ./scripts/spec.ps1 next pwsh ./scripts/spec.ps1 find registration pwsh ./scripts/spec.ps1 area portal next lists buildable candidates; it does not replace roadmap ordering. After changing feature status or discovery metadata, refresh and validate the generated feature index: pwsh ./scripts/spec.ps1 sync pwsh ./scripts/spec.ps1 health The generated catalog in spec/README.md must not be hand-edited. GitHub Actions runs the same health command for SDD-relevant pull requests and default-branch pushes. GitHub GitHub issues and projects are useful for discussion, prioritization, and traceability. They do not replace repository specs. Pull requests should link the relevant feature spec and confirm that: code matches the accepted specification; tenant isolation was reviewed; authorization was reviewed; catalog and tenant database impact was reviewed; DocFX documentation was updated or marked not applicable; generated API reference files were not manually edited. Before a local commit is created, the agent should summarize the changed files or feature areas, verification performed, checks not run, and proposed commit message. The commit should wait for explicit approval. Engineering Standards Feature implementation must follow rules.md, including the repository's C#/.NET architecture and coding standards. Apply SOLID principles pragmatically: keep services cohesive, preserve dependency direction, expose clear contracts at layer boundaries, and avoid abstractions that do not protect a real boundary or improve testability. Drift Handling When code and spec disagree, update the spec first or stop for a decision. Do not silently implement behavior that is missing from the spec.

articles/tenancy.html.title: Tenancy | Organizor
articles/tenancy.html.summary: Tenancy Organizor uses catalog-driven, database-per-tenant business data and realm-per-tenant identity data. The catalog database stores tenant records, plan assignment, config overrides, lifecycle status, soft-delete metadata, database name, and immutable IdentityRealm. Each active tenant has a dedicated PostgreSQL database named from its slug and a dedicated Keycloak realm named tenant-{normalized-slug}. One Keycloak deployment and database can host all of these realms. A separate Keycloak database per tenant is not required; the realm is the identity isolation boundary. Identity Topology Boundary Realm Contains Organizor control plane configured platform realm, organizor-dev locally Platform users, organizor-admin, central portal client. Tenant environment tenant-{slug} That tenant's users, credentials, sessions, roles, groups, website client, tenant-admin portal client, and API audience client. Provisioning only master Backend-only organizor-provisioner service account. PJsabbe and TVDK therefore have independent user identities. A person using both has two separate accounts and credentials; a username can be reused because Keycloak uniqueness is realm-local. Focused Guides Area Details Tenant catalog, statuses, header resolution, and database resolution Tenant Resolution Tenant request issuer binding Tenant Authorization Plans, overrides, effective config, and config API behavior Tenant Config Model Onboarding flow, tenant website auth settings, and deletion guardrails Tenant Onboarding Model Platform lifecycle endpoints Tenant Lifecycle Operations Keycloak realms, clients, and local bootstrap Keycloak Setup Rules Of Thumb Catalog operations use the catalog database. Tenant-scoped operations require X-Tenant-Slug unless the endpoint documents another tenant selection mechanism. Tenant-owned domain data lives in the resolved tenant database. The catalog is the source of truth for the tenant slug, database, and immutable Keycloak IdentityRealm mapping. Tenant realm roles and groups are local: /admins and /users, not a shared /tenants/{slug} hierarchy. API authentication accepts only the platform issuer or active catalog tenant issuers, then binds a tenant-scoped request to the resolved tenant realm. Tenant onboarding is the only workflow that creates catalog state, Keycloak realm access, and tenant database state together. The central portal host is a platform-realm control plane. A tenant-admin Portal host resolves its catalog-owned portal URL, tenant realm, and separate portal client before login. Runtime Shape flowchart LR Request["HTTP request"] Header["X-Tenant-Slug"] Catalog["Catalog DB: slug, database, IdentityRealm"] Context["ITenantContext"] TenantDb["Tenant PostgreSQL DB"] PlatformRealm["Platform realm\norganizor-admin"] TenantRealm["Tenant realm\ntenant-{slug}"] Request --> Header Header --> Catalog Catalog --> Context Context --> TenantDb PlatformRealm --> Request TenantRealm --> Request Context --> TenantRealm For a tenant-scoped authenticated request, the API accepts the tenant token only when its issuer is the realm held in the resolved tenant context. A platform organizor-admin is the explicit central-support exception where the endpoint policy permits it. Superseded shared-realm model: older historical material that refers to /tenants/{slug} Keycloak groups describes the prior implementation. New tenant onboarding uses a separate tenant realm and realm-local groups. Related Feature Areas User Capabilities Tenant Domain API Public Website API Database Provisioning

articles/tenant-authorization.html.title: Tenant Authorization | Organizor
articles/tenant-authorization.html.summary: Tenant Authorization Overview Tenant-scoped API routes require a valid bearer token and an X-Tenant-Slug header. The catalog maps that slug to a tenant database and an immutable Keycloak realm. The API then requires the token issuer to match that realm. Tenant Resolution Tenant-scoped routes include: X-Tenant-Slug: acme Resolution reads the active catalog tenant and stores its id, slug, and IdentityRealm in the request tenant context. Platform routes, public routes, and health/documentation routes bypass tenant resolution. Enforcement Rules For a tenant-scoped route: a tenant-acme token may call only requests resolved as acme; a tenant-contoso token calling X-Tenant-Slug: acme receives 403 Forbidden; a platform-realm token is cross-tenant only when it carries organizor-admin; the old no-tenant-claim superadmin bypass does not exist; the tenant claim is informational compatibility data, not an access decision; an organizor-api service-account token does not bypass issuer binding merely because it is a service account. Middleware Chain flowchart TD A[Request with X-Tenant-Slug] --> B[Tenant resolution] B --> C[Trusted multi-issuer authentication] C --> D[Issuer-to-tenant access binding] D --> E[Issuer-aware role policy] E --> F[Controller] HTTP Test Matrix Scenario Token issuer Header Expected PJsabbe user calls PJsabbe tenant-pjsabbe pjsabbe Allowed with required role PJsabbe user calls TVDK tenant-pjsabbe tvdk 403 Forbidden Platform admin supports TVDK platform realm + organizor-admin tvdk Allowed where policy permits Tenant role named organizor-admin calls platform route tenant realm none 403 Forbidden Soft-deleted tenant token disabled/removed tenant realm matching slug 401 Unauthorized Missing tenant header valid tenant token omitted 400 Bad Request

articles/tenant-config-model.html.title: Tenant Config Model | Organizor
articles/tenant-config-model.html.summary: Tenant Config Model Tenant configuration is catalog-owned. It combines system defaults, plan defaults, and tenant overrides into one effective config model. Important This page describes the legacy effective-configuration layer. It does not decide which product modules a tenant can use. Module deployment, plan entitlement, and tenant installation are separately managed through the Tenant Modules model. Plans And Overrides Tenant plans are persisted in the catalog database through the tenant_plans table. A plan defines default feature flags and structured settings for tenants assigned to that plan. Each tenant stores the following compatibility configuration: Field Purpose PlanKey Stable key of the selected plan, such as starter or pro. Features Tenant-level legacy feature flag overrides stored as PostgreSQL jsonb. It is not module entitlement. Settings Tenant-level structured setting overrides stored as PostgreSQL jsonb. It is not module installation state. Each plan stores: Field Purpose Key Stable plan identifier referenced by tenants. Name Human-readable plan name. Description Optional operator-facing description. Features Plan default legacy feature flags stored as PostgreSQL jsonb. It is not module entitlement. Settings Plan default structured settings stored as PostgreSQL jsonb. It is not module configuration unless an owning typed contract validates it. IsActive Whether the plan can be assigned. SortOrder Display ordering for future admin UI surfaces. Startup seeding keeps the initial plans available. It creates missing plan definitions but does not overwrite existing operator-managed plan metadata, legacy configuration, or module entitlements: Plan key Intent starter Default plan for new tenants with conservative limits. pro Larger customer plan with higher limits and self-service registration. limits.maxUsers = 0 means unlimited users for the assigned plan. The system default limits.maxUsers = 5 remains a fallback only. The starter and pro plans also have separate module bundles. The starter plan includes activities and offers the other initial modules as add-ons; pro includes the full family-activity bundle. See Tenant Modules. Effective Config ITenantConfigResolver resolves runtime config by tenant id or tenant slug. Effective config is built in this order: SystemDefaults -> PlanDefaults -> TenantOverrides Later layers override earlier layers. The returned model contains: Field Purpose TenantId Catalog tenant identifier. TenantSlug Stable tenant slug. PlanKey Assigned plan key. PlanName Assigned plan name. Features Effective flat feature flag dictionary. Settings Effective structured JSON settings object. Legacy feature merge rules: feature dictionaries are flat; plan defaults override system defaults by key; tenant overrides override plan defaults by key; missing keys do not remove earlier defaults. Settings merge rules: JSON objects are deep-merged; scalar values replace earlier scalar or object values; arrays replace earlier arrays; type conflicts are replaced by the later layer; JSON null values are preserved as explicit override values. Failure behavior: Condition Result error code Tenant does not exist or is soft-deleted TENANT_NOT_FOUND Assigned plan key does not resolve TENANT_PLAN_NOT_FOUND Assigned plan is inactive TENANT_PLAN_INACTIVE Tenant Config API Tenant admins fetch effective config for their current tenant: GET /api/v1/tenant/config Authorization: Bearer <tenant-admin-token> X-Tenant-Slug: acme Platform administrators inspect a tenant directly: GET /api/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/config Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> See Tenant Config Operations for platform admin update endpoints.

articles/tenant-config-operations.html.title: Tenant Config Operations | Organizor
articles/tenant-config-operations.html.summary: Tenant Config Operations All admin endpoints on this page require a bearer token satisfying the organizor-admin role policy. Important These compatibility routes manage effective legacy configuration and plan assignment. They do not install, enable, disable, or entitle modules. Use Tenant Modules for module lifecycle operations. Effective Config GET /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Returns effective config for one tenant. Effective config is resolved from system defaults, the tenant's assigned plan defaults, and tenant-level overrides. Tenant admins can view their own effective config through the tenant-scoped endpoint: GET /api/v1/tenant/config Authorization: Bearer <tenant-admin-token> X-Tenant-Slug: acme Tenant Overrides GET /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config-overrides Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Returns only explicit tenant-level overrides. PUT /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config-overrides Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Content-Type: application/json { "planKey": "pro", "features": { "branding.customLogo": true }, "settings": { "limits": { "maxUsers": 25 } } } Override updates replace the tenant's full assigned plan key, legacy feature override dictionary, and setting override dictionary. Omitted override keys are removed and inherited again from the assigned plan or system defaults. Changing planKey can change which modules are entitled, but it does not silently install or remove a tenant module; an incompatible active installation causes a plan-module conflict until an operator resolves it. Tenant Plans GET /api/admin/tenant-plans Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Returns available tenant plans and their default legacy feature settings. Retrieve and manage the plan's module bundle through the dedicated module-entitlement routes documented in Tenant Modules. PUT /api/admin/tenant-plans/{planKey} Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Content-Type: application/json { "name": "Pro", "description": "Larger customer plan with higher limits and self-service registration.", "features": { "registration.selfService": true }, "settings": { "limits": { "maxUsers": 0, "maxCamps": 25 } }, "isActive": true, "sortOrder": 20 } Plan updates replace editable metadata, legacy feature defaults, setting defaults, active state, and sort order. Existing tenant overrides remain intact. Module entitlements are a separate atomic operation so arbitrary feature JSON cannot become the module system.

articles/tenant-domain-api.html.title: Tenant Domain API | Organizor
articles/tenant-domain-api.html.summary: Tenant Domain API Tenant domain endpoints are tenant-scoped and require: Authorization: Bearer <token> X-Tenant-Slug: <tenant-slug> Unless stated otherwise, these endpoints require a token satisfying the tenant-admin role policy and tenant access middleware verifies that the user belongs to the tenant selected by the header. People And Relationships Relationship direction is from the responsible/contact person to the child or related person: fromPersonId: parent, guardian, emergency contact, or other responsible person. toPersonId: child participant or related person. Supported relationship types are Parent, Guardian, Mother, Father, StepParent, EmergencyContact, and Other. Endpoint Purpose GET /api/v1/people List tenant-local people. POST /api/v1/people Create a tenant-local person. PUT /api/v1/people/{personId} Update a tenant-local person. POST /api/v1/people/{personId}/link-user Link a tenant-local person to an existing tenant user id. POST /api/v1/people/{personId}/unlink-user Clear the tenant user link for a person. GET /api/v1/people/{personId}/relationships List relationships connected to a person. POST /api/v1/people/{personId}/relationships Create a relationship from personId to the request target. PUT /api/v1/people/{personId}/relationships/{relationshipId} Update relationship type and flags. POST /api/v1/people/{personId}/relationships/{relationshipId}/activate Mark a relationship active. POST /api/v1/people/{personId}/relationships/{relationshipId}/deactivate Mark a relationship inactive. POST /api/v1/people/{personId}/relationships/{relationshipId}/archive Archive a relationship. GET /api/v1/me/children List active children managed by the current linked parent or guardian person. Relationship validation returns stable error codes: Error Meaning PERSON_NOT_FOUND The route or request person does not exist in the resolved tenant database. PERSON_LINKED_USER_ID_REQUIRED The link request did not include a non-blank linked user id. PERSON_LINKED_USER_CONFLICT The linked user id is already assigned to another person in the tenant. PERSON_RELATIONSHIP_NOT_FOUND The requested relationship does not exist for the route person. PERSON_RELATIONSHIP_SELF_REFERENCE The source and target person are the same. PERSON_RELATIONSHIP_ALREADY_EXISTS An active relationship with the same source, target, and type already exists. PERSON_RELATIONSHIP_PRIMARY_CONTACT_CONFLICT The child already has an active primary-contact relationship. PERSON_RELATIONSHIP_INVALID The relationship request is invalid. Organizations Tenant organizations are tenant-local records used by activity setup and document capability eligibility. Endpoint Purpose GET /api/v1/organizations List tenant-local organizations. POST /api/v1/organizations Create a tenant-local organization. PUT /api/v1/organizations/{id} Update a tenant-local organization. Organization records include name, type, status, contact fields, optional KBO number and bank account, and structured address data. Activity Setup Endpoint Purpose GET /api/v1/activity-types List activity types. POST /api/v1/activity-types Create an activity type. PUT /api/v1/activity-types/{id} Update an activity type. POST /api/v1/activity-types/{id}/activate Activate an activity type. POST /api/v1/activity-types/{id}/deactivate Deactivate an activity type. POST /api/v1/activity-types/{id}/fields Create a registration field definition. PUT /api/v1/activity-types/{id}/fields/{fieldId} Update a registration field definition. GET /api/v1/activities List activities. POST /api/v1/activities Create an activity. PUT /api/v1/activities/{id} Update an activity. POST /api/v1/activities/{id}/activate Activate an activity. POST /api/v1/activities/{id}/deactivate Deactivate an activity. Activities can reference an activity type and optionally a tenant-local organization. Tenant admins can configure public activity page content separately from operational activity setup: Endpoint Purpose GET /api/v1/activities/{id}/public-detail Load tenant-admin public detail content JSON for one activity. PUT /api/v1/activities/{id}/public-detail Replace tenant-admin public detail content JSON for one activity. GET /api/v1/activity-public-page-templates List backend-provided public page templates. POST /api/v1/activities/{id}/public-detail/apply-template Replace one activity's public detail content with an editable copy of a template. GET /api/v1/public/activities/{activityId} Anonymous public-safe activity detail response for separate public websites. The public detail response contains a fixed hero object for the activity page, followed by ordered content blocks. The hero uses activity defaults unless tenant admins enable a hero override in the portal. Supported first-slice block types include richText, practicalInfo, schedule, tabs, faq, testimonial, gallery, and registrationCta; new authoring should prefer practical information tabs over standalone tabs, with those tabs presented above the general information rows. Gallery blocks may include a displayMode of grid or slideshow. Registration CTA blocks should render a visible registration action. Public websites should render hero before ordered blocks and ignore unknown future block types. Public page templates are backend-owned presets that use the same public detail block JSON contract. The current catalog exposes one standard activity page template for the TVDK-style public website layout. Applying a template copies the template content into the activity; the activity then owns its editable content independently from later template changes. Template listing is tenant-admin authorized but does not require tenant database resolution because templates are static backend presets. Applying a template remains tenant-scoped and requires the selected tenant context. Registration Validation Rules Validation rules are configured per activity type or per activity. Activity-level rules replace activity-type rules when they use the same rule key. The current slice stores these rules in the existing tenant JSON configuration fields instead of a separate table. Supported rule types: required required-when age-range regex numeric-range accepted-boolean required-when condition values are fixed to: present missing Supported targets are limited to core registration fields in this slice: participant data such as participant.firstName, participant.lastName, participant.email, participant.phoneNumber, participant.dateOfBirth, participant.address, and participant.nationalNumber contact data such as contact.firstName, contact.lastName, contact.email, contact.phoneNumber, contact.dateOfBirth, contact.address, and contact.nationalNumber registration.linkedUserId Endpoint Purpose GET /api/v1/activity-types/{activityTypeId}/registration-validation-rules Load activity-type validation rules. PUT /api/v1/activity-types/{activityTypeId}/registration-validation-rules Replace activity-type validation rules. GET /api/v1/activities/{activityId}/registration-validation-rules Load activity validation rules. PUT /api/v1/activities/{activityId}/registration-validation-rules Replace activity validation rules. Public registration submissions reject invalid payloads with REGISTRATION_VALIDATION_FAILED and a structured violations extension payload. Invalid rule configuration is rejected with REGISTRATION_RULE_INVALID, REGISTRATION_RULE_CONFLICT, or REGISTRATION_RULE_FIELD_UNKNOWN before the rules are saved. Registration Confirmation Email Tenant admins can configure confirmation email templates for activity types and activity-specific overrides. Activity templates override activity-type templates for the same culture. If no enabled template exists, public registration succeeds and returns confirmationStatus as not_configured. Confirmation templates are stored in the shared tenant email_templates table with purpose RegistrationConfirmation; delivery attempts are stored in email_deliveries with the same purpose. For child or dependent registrations, the default recipient is the active primary parent or guardian. Until every public registration creates structured parent/guardian relationships, confirmation rendering can fall back to submitted parent data in Registration.CoreDataJson: parentFirstName parentLastName parentEmail parentPhone Templates support double-brace variables such as {{participant.fullName}}, {{contact.fullName}}, {{activity.name}}, {{registration.paymentStatus}}, and {{tenant.slug}}. Unknown variables are rejected when saving, previewing, or sending. HTML templates reject unsafe script, event handler, JavaScript URL, form, and iframe content. Endpoint Purpose GET /api/v1/activity-types/{activityTypeId}/confirmation-templates List activity-type confirmation templates. PUT /api/v1/activity-types/{activityTypeId}/confirmation-templates/{culture} Create or update an activity-type template. GET /api/v1/activities/{activityId}/confirmation-templates List activity override templates. PUT /api/v1/activities/{activityId}/confirmation-templates/{culture} Create or update an activity override template. DELETE /api/v1/activities/{activityId}/confirmation-templates/{culture} Delete an activity override template. POST /api/v1/registrations/{registrationId}/confirmation-email/preview Render a confirmation email without sending it. POST /api/v1/registrations/{registrationId}/confirmation-email/send-test Send a test email and log the attempt. POST /api/v1/registrations/{registrationId}/confirmation-email/resend Send the confirmation email again and log the attempt. GET /api/v1/registrations/{registrationId}/confirmation-email/deliveries List confirmation delivery attempts for a registration. POST /api/v1/activities/{activityId}/public-registrations attempts confirmation delivery after the registration is persisted. Delivery failure does not roll back registration creation. The public response includes confirmationStatus with one of: not_configured sent failed Confirmation email uses the same tenant SMTP settings as document delivery under settings.email.smtp. SMTP credentials are never returned by confirmation endpoints. Preview intentionally returns rendered content and is restricted to tenant admins.
