Registrations Endpoint Purpose GET /api/v1/activities/{activityId}/registrations List registrations for an activity. GET /api/v1/registrations/{id} Load one registration. POST /api/v1/registrations/{id}/confirm Confirm a submitted registration. POST /api/v1/registrations/{id}/cancel Cancel a registration. POST /api/v1/registrations/{id}/mark-paid Mark a registration paid. POST /api/v1/registrations/{id}/mark-unpaid Mark a registration unpaid. POST /api/v1/activities/{activityId}/public-registrations Submit a public participant registration. Rate limited with PUBLIC_FORM_RATE_LIMITED when excessive anonymous submissions are detected. POST /api/v1/activities/{activityId}/registrations/for-child Submit a parent-managed registration for a managed child. GET /api/v1/me/activities List active activities available to the current tenant user. GET /api/v1/me/activity-types List active activity types and fields available to the current tenant user. Cancelled registrations reject later confirmation and payment updates. Parent-managed registrations require the current linked user to resolve to a parent or guardian person and to have an active relationship to the selected child with CanManageRegistrations set to true. The participant stays the child person; the linked user stays the parent or guardian account. Registrations reject a second non-cancelled registration for the same person and activity with REGISTRATION_ALREADY_EXISTS. A cancelled registration does not block a later registration. Activities with positive capacity reject new public and parent-managed registrations once the non-cancelled registration count reaches capacity. Capacity 0 is treated as unlimited. Full activities return ACTIVITY_CAPACITY_FULL. These parent-managed endpoints require the tenant-user role. Tenant admin rights alone do not grant child registration access. Document Capabilities The first supported capability keys are: fiscal-attestation healthcare-attestation Capabilities are assigned per activity type. Assignments are stored as tenant-local normalized data with optional optionsJson for capability-specific template or display configuration. Endpoint Purpose GET /api/v1/activity-types/{activityTypeId}/document-capabilities List document capabilities configured for an activity type. PUT /api/v1/activity-types/{activityTypeId}/document-capabilities Replace document capability assignments for an activity type. GET /api/v1/registrations/{registrationId}/document-eligibility Evaluate enabled document capabilities for a registration. GET /api/v1/registrations/{registrationId}/documents/{capabilityKey}/download Generate and download a PDF for an enabled document capability. POST /api/v1/registrations/{registrationId}/documents/{capabilityKey}/send Generate and email a PDF for an enabled document capability. Eligibility is evaluated on demand. It returns one result per enabled capability with: isEligible stable missingDataCodes stable blockingReasonCodes Fiscal and healthcare eligibility require the activity to have ended, the registration to be non-cancelled, complete child person data, a primary active parent/guardian relationship when parent data is required, and the connected organization data required by the selected capability. Document download and delivery currently support fiscal-attestation and healthcare-attestation. Generation is tenant-local, returns application/pdf, and does not persist generated documents. The backend fills PJSabbe-compatible PDF templates from the runtime documents folder: template_fiscalefiche_{activityStartYear}.pdf for fiscal attestations and template_healthcare_2024.pdf for healthcare attestations. Structured parent or guardian data from active primary person relationships takes precedence. Until all registrations have structured relationship data, generation can also read temporary parent data from Registration.CoreDataJson with: parentFirstName parentLastName parentDateOfBirth parentNationalNumber parentEmail parentAddress Document delivery uses effective tenant configuration under settings.email.smtp: { "email": { "smtp": { "host": "smtp.gmail.com", "port": 465, "useSsl": true, "senderEmail": "noreply@example.org", "senderName": "Example Club", "username": "noreply@example.org", "password": "<tenant-smtp-secret>" } } } Use tenant overrides or deployment secrets for SMTP credentials. Do not commit real provider secrets to appsettings files. Address objects must include street, number, zipCode or postalCode, city, and countryCode or country. Error Meaning DOCUMENT_CAPABILITY_INVALID The capability key, duplicate assignment, or options JSON is invalid. DOCUMENT_CAPABILITY_NOT_FOUND A requested capability key is not configured or not supported. DOCUMENT_CAPABILITY_REQUIRES_UNIMPLEMENTED_DATA A capability requires data owned by an unimplemented feature. DOCUMENT_GENERATION_NOT_ELIGIBLE The registration or activity state blocks generation. The detail includes stable blocking reason codes. DOCUMENT_REQUIRED_DATA_MISSING Required data is missing for generation. The detail includes stable missing-data codes. DOCUMENT_TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND The selected generation template cannot be resolved. DOCUMENT_DELIVERY_RECIPIENT_MISSING The parent or guardian email address is missing or invalid. DOCUMENT_DELIVERY_FAILED SMTP delivery failed. EMAIL_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED Tenant SMTP settings are missing or incomplete. CONFIRMATION_TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND No enabled confirmation template exists for the activity/culture. CONFIRMATION_TEMPLATE_INVALID Required template fields or reply-to email are invalid. CONFIRMATION_TEMPLATE_VARIABLE_INVALID The template contains an unsupported variable. CONFIRMATION_TEMPLATE_HTML_UNSAFE The HTML body contains unsafe content. CONFIRMATION_RECIPIENT_MISSING A valid confirmation recipient email cannot be resolved. CONFIRMATION_DELIVERY_FAILED SMTP confirmation delivery failed. ACTIVITY_TYPE_NOT_FOUND The activity type does not exist in the resolved tenant database. REGISTRATION_NOT_FOUND The registration does not exist in the resolved tenant database.

articles/tenant-lifecycle-operations.htm.title: Tenant Lifecycle Operations | Organizor
articles/tenant-lifecycle-operations.htm.summary: Tenant Lifecycle Operations All endpoints on this page require a token issued by the configured platform realm with the organizor-admin role. A tenant-realm role with the same text cannot access these operations. The platform administrator uses one control-plane login. The API uses its backend-only organizor-provisioner service account in Keycloak master to carry out realm lifecycle operations; no tenant or platform browser receives that secret. Onboard Tenant POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard Authorization: Bearer <platform-organizor-admin-token> Content-Type: application/json { "name": "Acme", "slug": "acme", "tenantAdminPortalBaseUrl": "https://admin.acme.example.com", "authSettings": { "websiteBaseUrl": "https://acme.example.com", "loginRedirectUris": ["https://acme.example.com/authentication/login-callback"], "logoutRedirectUris": ["https://acme.example.com"], "webOrigins": ["https://acme.example.com"], "registrationRedirectUrl": "https://acme.example.com/register/complete" } } The onboarding flow normalizes the slug, assigns immutable catalog realm tenant-acme, validates tenant website/auth and tenant-admin portal URLs, stores centralized auth settings plus the unique catalog portal URL, creates the catalog tenant as Pending, provisions the tenant Keycloak realm, creates the tenant database, applies tenant migrations, and marks the tenant Active on success. Realm provisioning creates realm-local tenant-admin and tenant-user roles, /admins and /users groups, an organizor-api audience client, separate tenant website and tenant-admin portal clients, and the default tenant administrator. The website and portal public auth contracts then return https://<keycloak>/realms/tenant-acme, not the platform realm. URL validation rejects wildcards, requires absolute HTTPS URLs, and allows HTTP only for local development hosts such as localhost and 127.0.0.1. Web origins must be origins only. Query Tenants GET /api/admin/tenants Authorization: Bearer <platform-organizor-admin-token> Returns all tenant catalog records, including soft-deleted tenants. GET /api/admin/tenants/{id} Authorization: Bearer <platform-organizor-admin-token> Returns one tenant by catalog ID, including soft-deleted records. The catalog-owned identity realm is an internal immutable lifecycle mapping, not editable tenant configuration. Upgrade Tenant POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/upgrade Authorization: Bearer <platform-organizor-admin-token> Runs pending migrations for the tenant database. Example response: { "database": "organizor_tenant_acme", "success": true, "appliedMigrations": 2, "duration": "00:00:01.2340000", "error": null } Soft Delete Tenant DELETE /api/admin/tenants/{id} Authorization: Bearer <platform-organizor-admin-token> Content-Type: application/json { "reason": "Customer cancellation" } Soft deletion first disables the tenant's complete Keycloak realm. Only after that succeeds does Organizor mark the catalog tenant as deleted, store deletion metadata, and set status to Deleted. The tenant database is not dropped. If Keycloak cannot disable the realm, the catalog tenant remains undeleted and the operation returns TENANT_IDENTITY_PROVIDER_FAILED. A soft-deleted tenant is removed from the API issuer allow-list, so an already-issued token from its realm is rejected immediately. Hard Delete Tenant POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/hard-delete Authorization: Bearer <platform-organizor-admin-token> Hard deletion requires the tenant to already be soft-deleted. It performs cleanup in this order: Delete the complete tenant realm, including users, sessions, groups, roles, website clients, and API audience client. Drop the tenant database. Remove the catalog record. A missing tenant realm is treated as already deleted, allowing retry of a partially completed cleanup. If realm deletion fails, the API returns TENANT_IDENTITY_PROVIDER_FAILED and does not drop the database or remove the catalog record.

articles/tenant-modules.html.title: Tenant Modules | Organizor
articles/tenant-modules.html.summary: Tenant Modules Organizor is a modular monolith: one deployed API and one database-per-tenant platform, with a code-owned module catalog. It does not load third-party assemblies at runtime or split every module into a microservice. A module answers a product-composition question: which business workflows a tenant can use. It is deliberately separate from tenant settings, user roles, and sport labels. Five Separate Concerns Question Owner Source of truth Is code available in this deployment? Module registry Compiled, startup-registered module definition. Is the module part of a plan or available as an add-on? Tenant plan Plan-module entitlement. Has a tenant activated the module? Tenant installation Tenant-module installation record. May a user perform an action? Authorization and tenant access Existing roles and tenant-access checks. How should an active module behave? Module-owned configuration Typed, validated configuration contract. A module is available to tenant-owned behavior only when its code is deployed, the tenant plan entitles it, the tenant has an installation record in Enabled state, and all of its dependencies are enabled. API enforcement is server-side; hiding a portal navigation item is not security. The first foundation slice exposes the reusable availability gate, but does not retroactively gate every existing compatibility endpoint. Existing module-owned endpoints are attached to the gate in their own rollout work so existing tenants are not silently broken before their installation state is explicitly configured. Module Catalog The initial catalog is organized by business workflow, not by sport or customer brand. Key Purpose Required modules activities Activity types, activities, schedules, pricing, capacity, and public activity content. None registrations Registration forms, validation, capacity, status, payment tracking, and confirmations. activities participants-families People, guardian/parent-child relationships, contact responsibility, and reusable family data. None parent-self-service Guardian access to managed children, child registration, registration visibility, and permitted cancellation. registrations, participants-families organizations Tenant organization records, including legal issuer data used by qualifying workflows. None attestations Activity-type attestation eligibility and fiscal or healthcare document workflows. activities, registrations, participants-families, organizations Football, swimming, camps, training, and EAD lessons are tenant-local activity types and activity configuration. They are not modules. PJsabbe and TVDK therefore use the same full bundle: activities registrations participants-families parent-self-service organizations attestations They differ through their activity types, organization/legal-issuer data, public content, and other typed tenant settings. A future tenant can select a smaller compatible bundle, such as activities alone or activities and registrations. Plans And Tenant Installations A plan has one entitlement for every deployed module: Entitlement Meaning Included The plan supplies the module. It is installed automatically during successful onboarding. Optional A platform administrator can install it later as a tenant add-on. Unavailable The plan cannot activate the module. The seeded plans are intentionally simple: Plan Included modules Add-ons starter activities All other initial modules are optional. pro The full PJsabbe/TVDK family-activity bundle. None in the initial catalog. Each tenant installation records its source (PlanIncluded or PlanAddOn) and its state: State Meaning Installing Installation has started. If an interruption leaves it in this state, an operator can retry it. Enabled The module can be used, subject to normal authorization. Disabled The module is intentionally inactive; its business data is retained. Failed Installation failed and records a machine-readable reason; an operator can retry it. Installing a module requires an active tenant, a plan entitlement, and enabled dependencies. A tenant whose provisioning completed but whose included modules failed can recover only its included modules until the full included bundle is enabled. An enabled module cannot be disabled while another enabled module depends on it. Re-enabling preserves module business data. Changing a plan entitlement to Unavailable is blocked while an enabled, failed, or installing non-exception tenant installation still uses that entitlement; disable the module first or choose a compatible plan. Onboarding POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard accepts an optional planKey. When omitted, Organizor uses starter. The requested plan must exist and be active. { "name": "TVDK", "slug": "tvdk", "planKey": "pro", "authSettings": { "websiteBaseUrl": "https://www.example.org" } } After Keycloak provisioning, tenant database creation, and tenant migrations succeed, Organizor installs every included module in dependency order. Optional modules remain a deliberate platform-admin action. If included-module installation fails, the tenant is marked Failed with a recoverable module-installation reason; the platform admin can repair and retry its included modules, and the tenant becomes active once they are all enabled. A failed tenant onboarding does not make its modules available. Existing tenants are not inferred from legacy feature flags or JSON settings. A platform administrator configures their installations explicitly during the transition. Platform Operator API All module-management routes are catalog-scoped, require organizor-admin, and do not use X-Tenant-Slug. Inspect the deployed catalog GET /api/admin/modules Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Returns every code-deployed module with its stable key, display metadata, version, and dependencies. Manage plan bundles GET /api/admin/tenant-plans/{planKey}/module-entitlements PUT /api/admin/tenant-plans/{planKey}/module-entitlements Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> The PUT body replaces the plan's complete entitlement set atomically. It must include every deployed module and use Included, Optional, or Unavailable for each one. { "modules": [ { "moduleKey": "activities", "availability": "Included" }, { "moduleKey": "registrations", "availability": "Optional" }, { "moduleKey": "participants-families", "availability": "Optional" }, { "moduleKey": "parent-self-service", "availability": "Optional" }, { "moduleKey": "organizations", "availability": "Optional" }, { "moduleKey": "attestations", "availability": "Optional" } ] } Manage a tenant's installed modules GET /api/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/modules POST /api/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/modules/{moduleKey}/install POST /api/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/modules/{moduleKey}/retry POST /api/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/modules/{moduleKey}/enable POST /api/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/modules/{moduleKey}/disable Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> The list response provides each module's plan availability, installation state/source/failure reason, dependency state, and the actions currently permitted to the operator. Install, retry, enable, and disable return the updated module record. Relevant stable errors include TENANT_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, TENANT_MODULE_NOT_ENTITLED, TENANT_MODULE_DEPENDENCY_NOT_ENABLED, TENANT_MODULE_INVALID_STATE, TENANT_MODULE_PLAN_CONFLICT, and TENANT_MODULE_TENANT_NOT_ACTIVE. Platform Portal Workflow The platform portal presents module lifecycle in plain language: The Plans page has a Modules tab where an Organizor admin selects Included, Optional add-on, or Unavailable for every deployed module. The tenant onboarding dialog lists active plans and sends the chosen planKey. The tenant detail drawer has a Modules section showing entitlement, installation state, source, dependencies, and a contextual Install, Retry, Enable, or Disable action. Tenant administrators continue to manage only the typed settings that an enabled module explicitly delegates to them. They do not manage plan entitlements or tenant module lifecycle. Configuration And Legacy JSON The existing tenant_plans.features, tenant_plans.settings, tenants.features, and tenants.settings JSONB-backed configuration remains supported as a compatibility layer. It still supplies effective legacy config through the existing system defaults -> plan defaults -> tenant overrides merge. That JSON is not the module system: Do not use a generic feature flag to decide whether a tenant has a module. Do not store module installation state, entitlement, authorization, queryable limits, or secrets in an arbitrary JSON editor. Use a typed, validated module contract for settings owned by a module. Bounded, validated JSONB can still be appropriate for optional module settings, but it never determines module availability. SMTP and OIDC are integrations with typed configuration and write-only/redacted secrets; they are not sellable modules. The first migration preserves existing JSON values and does not reinterpret them as installations. A later migration will classify each existing feature flag as a temporary release flag, module entitlement, module setting, or obsolete configuration before retirement. Catalog Persistence Module lifecycle metadata lives in the catalog database; module business data remains in the tenant database. Table Key columns Purpose tenant_plan_module_entitlements plan_key, module_key, availability, timestamps One entitlement per deployed module for each plan. plan_key references tenant_plans.key. tenant_module_installations tenant_id, module_key, state, source, failure_reason, timestamps One lifecycle record per installed tenant module. tenant_id references tenants.id. Both tables use composite primary keys of their two identity columns. Deleting a plan or tenant cascades its matching catalog module metadata. The installation table is indexed by tenant and state for operator and availability lookups. Startup seeding creates missing initial plans and missing entitlement rows, but does not overwrite operator-managed plan metadata, settings, or entitlement choices. Relationship To Activity Attestations The attestations module enables the capability family, but it does not make every activity eligible. Tenant administrators configure fiscal and healthcare capabilities per activity type. For the PJsabbe and TVDK composition, eligible camps can enable attestations while football, swimming, and EAD training types remain ineligible unless their own accepted rules say otherwise. Historical registration and attestation input must be preserved when people or guardian relationships later change. The separate PJsabbe import and historical snapshot migration is deferred to its own feature. For effective configuration details, see Tenant Config Model. For the broader onboarding workflow, see Tenant Onboarding Model.

articles/tenant-onboarding-model.html.title: Tenant Onboarding Model | Organizor
articles/tenant-onboarding-model.html.summary: Tenant Onboarding Model The preferred full tenant creation route is: POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard It creates the catalog record, assigns an immutable tenant Keycloak realm, stores centralized website/auth settings and a tenant-admin portal base URL, provisions tenant identity resources, creates the tenant database, applies migrations, installs the selected plan's included modules, and marks the tenant Active only after the workflow succeeds. Catalog Identity Mapping Every tenant owns one Keycloak realm. The catalog assigns Tenant.IdentityRealm deterministically as tenant-{normalized-slug} before the tenant is persisted: Tenant Slug Identity realm PJsabbe pjsabbe tenant-pjsabbe TVDK tvdk tenant-tvdk Acme acme tenant-acme IdentityRealm is a required, unique, immutable catalog field. AdminPortalBaseUrl is a nullable, unique catalog field: catalog-only creation may leave it empty, but full onboarding requires it. Neither is an editable tenant JSON setting or inferred from a token or HTTP request. Flow flowchart TD A[Onboard request] --> B[Create catalog tenant as Pending with IdentityRealm] B --> C[Store centralized website/auth settings] C --> D[Create or reuse tenant Keycloak realm] D --> E[Create realm-local roles and /admins,/users groups] E --> F[Create API-audience, tenant website, and tenant portal clients] F --> G[Create tenant database] G --> H[Apply tenant migrations] H --> I{Provisioning successful?} I -->|Yes| J[Mark tenant Active] J --> K[Install included modules] K --> L{Every included module enabled?} L -->|Yes| M[Create default realm-local tenant admin] M --> N[Onboarding succeeds] L -->|No| O[Mark tenant Failed: recoverable module failure] O --> P[Admin repairs and retries included modules] P --> L I -->|No| Q[Mark tenant Failed] The Keycloak provisioning token is obtained by the backend-only organizor-provisioner service account in the master realm. Platform administrators use their normal platform-realm login and do not receive Keycloak master credentials. Tenant Realm Contents For tenant acme, onboarding creates or reuses tenant-acme and ensures: realm roles tenant-admin and tenant-user; realm-local /admins and /users groups, mapped to those roles; the internal organizor-api audience client; public PKCE client tenant-acme-web; public PKCE client tenant-acme-portal; default tenant admin acme-admin in /admins. There is no /tenants/acme/... group hierarchy. The realm itself is the tenant boundary. The same username or email can therefore be used independently in different tenant realms. Initial Tenant Administrator Credential The default administrator is created only after tenant database provisioning and included-module installation both succeed. When it is newly created, the successful POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard response includes its username and temporary password once, with Cache-Control: no-store. The portal shows a copyable one-time notice. The credential is never stored in the catalog, tenant settings, logs, or tenant list responses; dismissing the notice removes it from the portal's in-memory page state. Creating or reusing an existing default administrator never resets its password and does not return a credential. If the response is lost after the Keycloak account was created, the password cannot be recovered. Likewise, a tenant whose module installation initially failed may later recover without an automatically issued default administrator. In either case, create a replacement realm-local tenant-admin through POST /api/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/users with a temporary password and required UPDATE_PASSWORD action. If the tenant user limit is one, remove the stranded default account before adding the replacement. This API recovery path also works while the tenant is Failed; the portal user-management screen selects active tenants only. Plan Selection And Included Modules The onboarding request accepts an optional planKey. When no plan key is supplied, Organizor assigns starter. The selected plan must be active. After provisioning succeeds, Organizor installs every module included by the selected plan in dependency order. Optional plan modules are not installed automatically; an Organizor administrator can add them later from the tenant module control plane. If included-module installation fails, the tenant is marked Failed with a recoverable module failure; only its included modules can be repaired, installed, re-enabled, or retried until the whole included bundle is enabled. Failed provisioning leaves the tenant inactive and its modules unavailable. The starter plan includes activities; the pro plan includes the full PJsabbe/TVDK family-activity bundle. Plan entitlement and tenant installation are separate from legacy features and settings JSON. See Tenant Modules for the catalog and operator workflow. Website And Auth Settings Onboarding accepts tenant website/auth settings for separate tenant UI projects: Field Purpose websiteBaseUrl Public tenant website base URL. loginRedirectUris OIDC login callback URLs allowed by the tenant website client. logoutRedirectUris Post-logout redirect URLs allowed by the tenant website client. webOrigins Browser origins allowed by the tenant website client. Defaults to the website origin when omitted. registrationRedirectUrl Optional tenant website URL used after registration flows. In the platform onboarding dialog, entering a valid websiteBaseUrl suggests editable values for the four related fields: {base}/authentication/login-callback, {base}, the website origin, and {base}/register/complete. The base path is retained in callback URLs, while the web origin contains only scheme, host, and optional port. A later base URL change updates only fields that still use a portal suggestion, so an operator's manual customization is preserved. Reset suggested values deliberately reapplies all four values from the current base URL. These values are stored in tenant settings under website and auth. Organizor also stores a generated auth.clientId using tenant-{slug}-web and provisions that public client in the tenant's own realm. The realm identifier itself remains the immutable relational Tenant.IdentityRealm, not JSON configuration. The tenant public client uses Authorization Code Flow with PKCE. It emits realm roles, aud: organizor-api, and a direct tenant claim containing the tenant slug for client compatibility. The API does not use the tenant claim to decide tenant access; it binds the JWT issuer to the catalog identity realm. Tenant websites must obtain their authority and client id from GET /api/public/tenants/{slug}/auth. Tenant Admin Portal URL Full onboarding also requires tenantAdminPortalBaseUrl, for example https://localhost:7022 for local TVDK administration. It is a normalized, unique HTTPS base URL (with the existing local HTTP allowance), stored relationally as AdminPortalBaseUrl rather than in tenant JSON settings. The platform onboarding form keeps it visibly separate from the public website base URL and does not infer a production admin host from that website. The URL provisions a separate tenant-{slug}-portal client in the tenant's own realm. Its only redirect URI is {portalBaseUrl}/authentication/login-callback; its post-logout redirect URI is {portalBaseUrl}; and its web origin is the portal URL origin. The client uses Authorization Code Flow with PKCE and the same realm-role, organizor-api audience, and direct tenant-claim mappers as the website client. At the tenant portal host, the Portal loads GET /api/public/tenant-portals/auth?baseUrl=... before OIDC startup. That contract returns public configuration only and must match the actual host exactly. The central platform host remains fixed to the platform realm and never chooses a tenant realm from a user input. Catalog-Only Creation POST /api/v1/tenants creates only the catalog record with Pending status and assigns its deterministic IdentityRealm. It does not create the Keycloak realm, users, groups, clients, or tenant database. Deletion Lifecycle Soft deletion first disables the tenant realm. If Keycloak cannot disable it, Organizor keeps the catalog tenant active and returns TENANT_IDENTITY_PROVIDER_FAILED. Once soft-deleted, the tenant is removed from the API issuer allow-list, so previously issued tenant tokens are rejected immediately. Hard deletion is intentionally guarded: the tenant must already be soft-deleted. The workflow executes in this order: Delete the complete tenant realm, including users, sessions, roles, groups, and clients. Drop the tenant database. Remove the catalog record. A missing tenant realm is treated as already deleted so a partial cleanup can be retried. If realm deletion fails, database and catalog deletion do not run and the operation returns TENANT_IDENTITY_PROVIDER_FAILED.

articles/tenant-resolution.html.title: Tenant Resolution | Organizor
articles/tenant-resolution.html.summary: Tenant Resolution Organizor uses catalog-driven, database-per-tenant tenancy. Tenant Catalog The catalog database stores tenant metadata through CatalogDbContext. Each tenant includes identity, slug, database name, plan key, overrides, lifecycle status, failure reason, and soft-delete metadata. The database name convention is: organizor_tenant_{slug} Slugs are normalized to lowercase before they are stored or used for lookups. Normal catalog reads exclude soft-deleted tenants. Internal operations can include soft-deleted records when explicitly required. Tenant Statuses Status Meaning Pending Tenant exists in the catalog but provisioning is not complete. Active Tenant provisioning completed successfully. Upgrading Reserved for upgrade lifecycle state. Failed Provisioning failed or an unexpected onboarding error occurred. Deleted Tenant has been soft-deleted. HTTP Tenant Resolution TenantResolutionMiddleware resolves tenant context for tenant-scoped routes. It skips platform endpoints such as: /api/admin /api/v1/tenants /health /scalar /openapi root and common static paths For tenant-scoped requests, clients must send: X-Tenant-Slug: acme The middleware loads the tenant from the catalog and stores TenantInfo in ITenantContext. If the header is missing, the response is 400 Bad Request. If the slug does not match a catalog tenant, the response is 404 Not Found. Tenant Database Resolution OrganizorDbContext uses a fallback in-memory database when no tenant has been resolved. This supports startup, Scalar, migrations, and design-time tooling. When a tenant is resolved, PerTenantDbResolver loads the catalog tenant, builds a PostgreSQL connection string for that tenant database, and OrganizorDbContext uses that database.

articles/user-capabilities.html.title: User Capabilities | Organizor
articles/user-capabilities.html.summary: User Capabilities Organizor separates platform administration, tenant administration, regular tenant-user access through tenant-specific public UIs, and anonymous public flows. Capability Matrix Capability Organizor admin Tenant admin Tenant user Anonymous View tenant catalog Yes No No No Create catalog tenant record Yes No No No Onboard, upgrade, soft-delete, or hard-delete tenants Yes No No No Manage tenant plan defaults Yes No No No Manage tenant plan module entitlements Yes No No No Manage tenant module installations Yes No No No Manage tenant config overrides from the platform control plane Yes No No No Manage users for a selected tenant from the platform control plane Yes No No No Manage users inside own tenant No Yes No No View own tenant effective config No Yes No No Manage people and relationships No Yes No No Manage organizations No Yes No No Manage activities and activity types No Yes No No Configure activity type document capabilities No Yes No No Review and update registrations No Yes No No View own profile No Yes Yes No Start own password-change flow No Yes Yes No Update own first and last name No Yes Yes No Resolve public tenant auth contract Yes Yes Yes Yes Self-register as tenant user No No No Yes, when enabled Platform Administrator Platform administrators carry organizor-admin in the platform realm. They operate across tenants from the platform control plane. They can create catalog tenant records, run full onboarding, upgrade tenant databases, soft-delete tenants, hard-delete previously soft-deleted tenants, manage tenant plan defaults and module entitlements, install or disable tenant modules, edit tenant config overrides, and manage tenant users for a selected active tenant. Tenant Administrator Tenant administrators carry tenant-admin in their own tenant realm and must match the tenant selected by X-Tenant-Slug. They can manage tenant users, config inspection, people, relationships, organizations, activity setup, registrations, document capability assignment, and their own profile actions. They cannot list/read the platform tenant catalog, alter a plan entitlement, or manage module installation lifecycle; enabled modules may delegate only their typed settings to tenant administrators. Tenant User Tenant users carry tenant-user in their own tenant realm and must match their tenant. They do not use the Organizor portal; profile display, password-change initiation, allowed profile field updates, family dashboard, and activity registration workflows belong in tenant-specific public UIs such as TVDK. Tenant users do not manage tenant config, users, activities, relationships, organizations, registrations, document capabilities, or tenant catalog visibility. Anonymous User Anonymous users can call only explicitly public endpoints. The current public flows are tenant auth discovery and tenant-user self-registration when registration is enabled for the tenant. Public activity registration submission is also anonymous but selects tenant context through the activity and public registration contract rather than through the portal's authenticated tenant header flow.

index.html.title: Organizor API | Organizor
index.html.summary:
Organizor API Organizor is a multi-tenant ASP.NET Core API for creating, provisioning, resolving, upgrading, and deleting tenant environments. Local Only The local development path uses HTTPS Keycloak at https://localhost:8443, the Blazor portal at https://localhost:7025, and the API at https://localhost:7184. Runtime Architecture flowchart LR Portal["Blazor Portal
https://localhost:7025"] Keycloak["Keycloak
OIDC + roles"] Api["Organizor API
tenant lifecycle"] Catalog["Catalog DB
tenant registry"] Tenants["Tenant DBs
database per tenant"] Portal -->|login + token| Keycloak Portal -->|Bearer token| Api Api -->|issuer metadata| Keycloak Api --> Catalog Api --> Tenants Note Conceptual docs explain behavior and workflows. The generated API reference is reserved for C# namespaces, types, methods, and signatures. Documentation Map Area Use it for Developer Guide Daily development loop, common commands, tenant headers, and doc editing rules. Features Overview Product capability map by platform, tenant, and public website area. User Capabilities Role-based matrix for platform admins, tenant admins, tenant users, and anonymous users. Getting Started Running the API locally and building the documentation. Local Development Canonical local topology, ports, startup order, and verification checklist. Portal UI Portal routes, layouts, and links to admin and tenant workflow pages. Architecture Understanding the API, application, domain, and infrastructure layers. Tenancy Tenant catalog, tenant resolution, provisioning, and database-per-tenant behavior. API Behavior Platform catalog routes, tenant config, utility endpoints, and links to feature API pages. Errors and Observability Correlation IDs, error responses, and logging context. Database Provisioning Catalog database, tenant databases, PostgreSQL permissions, extensions, and migrations. Configuration Connection strings, PostgreSQL settings, logging, CORS, OpenAPI, and Scalar. Keycloak HTTPS Local trusted HTTPS setup for Keycloak. Security CORS, admin route exposure, error detail, and destructive operation notes. Internal Operations Admin routes, tenant onboarding, upgrades, deletion, documentation deployment, and sitemap output. Solution Structure Code7Dev.Organizor.Api hosts the HTTP API, middleware, OpenAPI/Scalar setup, health checks, CORS, and logging pipeline. Code7Dev.Organizor.Application contains tenant use cases and service contracts. Code7Dev.Organizor.Domain contains the tenant aggregate and lifecycle status. Code7Dev.Organizor.Infrastructure contains EF Core persistence, PostgreSQL database provisioning, tenant database resolution, and migration support. Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui hosts the Blazor WebAssembly portal that authenticates with Keycloak and calls the API. Runtime Surface Endpoint Purpose /api/v1/tenants Public tenant catalog operations. /api/v1/tenant/config Tenant-scoped effective config for the current tenant. /api/admin/tenants Internal tenant onboarding, upgrades, deletion, effective config, and override operations. /api/admin/tenant-plans Internal tenant plan default management. /health Health checks. /openapi/v1.json OpenAPI document in development. /scalar Interactive OpenAPI/Scalar endpoint explorer in development. Start with the developer guide for day-to-day commands, then use the overview, public API behavior guide, and internal operations guide for workflows. Use the generated API reference only when you need C# type and member signatures.
